children.title: Generalized Disjunctive Programming
children.top_down_role: Logic-centered organization of global restrictions, algebraic alternatives, and Boolean relations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Boolean-trigger representation and disjunctive reformulation of GDP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simplified generalized disjunctive programming representation with exactly-one activation, additional Boolean conditions, and linear or convex nonlinear alternatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each alternative \(i\in Q\), associate a Boolean trigger \(Y_i\). A simplified GDP representation consists of \[\bigvee_{i\in Q}\begin{bmatrix}Y_i\\ A^i x\ge b^i\end{bmatrix},\qquad \text{exactly one }Y_i\text{ is true},\qquad \Omega((Y_i)_{i\in Q})=\mathrm{True}.\] The trigger activates or deactivates its associated constraint system, while \(\Omega\) specifies further logical conditions on the triggers. A linear GDP can be reformulated as a linear disjunctive program. If the linear systems are replaced by convex nonlinear systems \(G^i(x)\ge h^i\), the resulting GDP can be reformulated as a nonlinear disjunctive program. The disjunctive hull-relaxation procedure can also be adapted to this GDP representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a simplified generalized disjunctive program, each alternative has a Boolean trigger, exactly one trigger is true, and an additional Boolean condition can relate the triggers. Linear GDPs can be reformulated as linear disjunctive programs; GDPs with convex nonlinear alternatives can be reformulated as nonlinear disjunctive programs. The hull-relaxation procedure can be adapted to GDP models.
assumptions_latex: P^i=\{x:A^i x\ge b^i\}\quad\text{in the linear case}
G^i(x)\ge h^i\quad\text{defines a convex nonlinear alternative in the nonlinear case}
\Omega((Y_i)_{i\in Q})\text{ is a Boolean condition on the triggers}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The trigger-variable GDP is reformulable as a linear disjunctive program for linear alternatives and as a nonlinear disjunctive program for convex nonlinear alternatives; its hull relaxation can be adapted accordingly.}

children.top_down_role: Separation between shared model structure and alternative-local structure.

children.title: Global Structure
children.top_down_role: Model components shared across all disjunctive alternatives.

knowledge_statements.title: Global Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraints imposed independently of disjunct selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
In a generalized disjunctive program with continuous variables \(x\in X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) and Boolean selectors \(Y\), the global structure is the collection of constraints
\[g_r(x)\leq 0\quad(r\in R),\qquad \Omega(Y)=\mathrm{True},\]
that apply to every feasible solution rather than only within a particular disjunct. Thus the feasible set is intersected with \(G=\{x\in X:g_r(x)\leq0\text{ for all }r\in R\}\), regardless of which alternatives are active; \(\Omega\) may additionally restrict admissible selector combinations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Global structure consists of constraints that every solution must satisfy, regardless of which disjuncts are selected.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in G\) is required under every admissible selection \(Y\).

children.title: Disjunct-Local Structure
children.top_down_role: Restrictions or variables belonging to individual alternatives.

knowledge_statements.title: Disjunct-Local Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraints conditional on one alternative's activation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a disjunction \(q\) with alternatives \(k\in K_q\), disjunct-local structure consists of constraint systems \(h_{qkj}(x)\leq0\) indexed by \(j\in J_{qk}\) and attached only to selector \(Y_{qk}\). Their semantics are
\[Y_{qk}\Rightarrow h_{qkj}(x)\leq0\quad\text{for every }j\in J_{qk}.\]
When \(Y_{qk}\) is false, these local constraints impose no restriction unless they also appear in the global structure or in another active disjunct. The active local feasible set is \(D_{qk}=\{x:h_{qkj}(x)\leq0\text{ for all }j\in J_{qk}\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Disjunct-local constraints apply only when their associated Boolean alternative is active.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Y_{qk}=\mathrm{True}\Rightarrow x\in D_{qk}.\)

notation.meaning: selector for alternative k of disjunction q
local feasible set of the alternative

children.title: Shared-Variable Coupling
children.top_down_role: Interfaces linking alternative-local components through common variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Shared-Variable Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coupling induced when distinct disjuncts constrain common variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let active alternatives \(D_{qk}\) and \(D_{r\ell}\) be defined on a common variable vector \(x\in X\). If both selectors \(Y_{qk}\) and \(Y_{r\ell}\) are true, then the same value of \(x\) must satisfy both local systems:
\[x\in D_{qk}\cap D_{r\ell}.\]
Hence nonempty individual alternatives do not ensure joint feasibility: \(D_{qk}\neq\varnothing\) and \(D_{r\ell}\neq\varnothing\) may hold while \(D_{qk}\cap D_{r\ell}=\varnothing\). This intersection requirement is shared-variable coupling and prevents independent treatment of the two selections.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Active disjuncts sharing variables require one common assignment, so individually feasible alternatives may be jointly infeasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in D_{qk}\cap D_{r\ell}\), which may be empty.

notation.meaning: local feasible set for one alternative
local feasible set for another alternative

children.title: Locality Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Cases where model components cannot be cleanly assigned to global or local layers.

knowledge_statements.title: Locality Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions distinguishing disjunct-local enforcement from global or cross-alternative coupling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Y_{qk}\) be the Boolean selector for alternative \((q,k)\), and let \(c_{qk}(x)\leq 0\) be a constraint attached to that alternative. The constraint is disjunct-local when its semantics are
\[Y_{qk}\Rightarrow c_{qk}(x)\leq 0,\]
so it need not hold solely because \(Y_{qk}\) is false. The variables in \(x\) may be shared with other disjuncts; sharing variables alone does not make the constraint global. A constraint lies outside this local scope when it is enforced under every selection, governs selector combinations or several alternatives jointly, or supplies consistency relations between distinct local variable copies. Such restrictions belong to the global or coupling structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constraint is disjunct-local when its enforcement is conditional on one alternative; shared variables alone do not destroy locality, while unconditional or cross-alternative restrictions are global or coupling constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Y_{qk}\Rightarrow c_{qk}(x)\leq0\) expresses local enforcement; unconditional or joint enforcement crosses the locality boundary.

children.title: Boolean Selection Layers
children.top_down_role: Logical organization of alternative activation and interaction.

knowledge_statements.title: Boolean Selection Layers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boolean representation of disjunct activation and interaction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Y_{qk}\) select alternative \(k\in K_q\) of disjunction \(q\in Q\). A Boolean selection layer is a proposition
\[\Omega(Y)\wedge\bigwedge_{q\in Q}\left(\bigvee_{k\in K_q}Y_{qk}\right),\]
together with implications \(Y_{qk}\Rightarrow x\in D_{qk}\). If exactly one alternative is required in each disjunction, the clause for \(q\) is strengthened by pairwise exclusion, equivalently \(\sum_{k\in K_q}y_{qk}=1\) for binary encodings \(y_{qk}\). The global proposition \(\Omega(Y)\) expresses permitted or forbidden combinations across different disjunctions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Boolean layers select local alternatives and impose logical rules within and across disjunctions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Y_{qk}\Rightarrow x\in D_{qk}\), subject to the selection clauses and \(\Omega(Y)\).

notation.meaning: feasible set of alternative k in disjunction q

children.title: Trigger-Variable Disjunctions
children.top_down_role: Disjunctions controlled by external activation decisions.

knowledge_statements.title: Trigger-Variable Disjunctions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A disjunction activated conditionally by an external decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(z\in\{0,1\}\) be an external trigger and let \(D_1,\ldots,D_m\subseteq X\) be alternatives. A trigger-variable disjunction imposes
\[z=1\Rightarrow x\in\bigcup_{k=1}^mD_k.\]
Using binary alternative selectors \(y_k\), an exactly-one-when-triggered encoding satisfies \(\sum_{k=1}^m y_k=z\) and \(y_k=1\Rightarrow x\in D_k\) for every \(k\). Thus \(z=0\) deactivates all alternatives, whereas \(z=1\) activates exactly one. Any constraints required when \(z=0\) must be specified separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An external binary trigger activates a disjunction; selector sums can enforce exactly one active alternative only when the trigger is on.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{k=1}^m y_k=z\Rightarrow[z=0\Rightarrow y=0]\text{ and }[z=1\Rightarrow\sum_{k=1}^m y_k=1].\)

children.title: Generated Disjunction Hierarchy
children.top_down_role: Nested, repeated, and index-generated systems of alternatives.

children.title: Nested Disjunctions
children.top_down_role: Alternatives containing subordinate logical choices.

knowledge_statements.title: Nested Disjunctions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hierarchical alternatives whose activation exposes subordinate choices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A nested disjunction is a rooted finite selection hierarchy in which choosing a parent alternative conditionally activates a child disjunction. If \(Y_p\) selects a parent and \(Y_{pc}\) selects child \(c\in C(p)\), then the child selectors satisfy
\[Y_{pc}\Rightarrow Y_p\quad(c\in C(p)),\qquad Y_p\Rightarrow\bigvee_{c\in C(p)}Y_{pc}.\]
Under exactly-one child selection, binary encodings obey \(\sum_{c\in C(p)}y_{pc}=y_p\). Each selected node imposes its attached local constraints, so a feasible leaf selection satisfies every constraint along its root-to-leaf activation path.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Selecting a parent activates a subordinate choice, and a feasible leaf inherits all local constraints along its hierarchy path.
assumptions_latex: the selection hierarchy is finite and rooted
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{c\in C(p)}y_{pc}=y_p\) enforces exactly one selected child precisely when parent \(p\) is selected.

notation.meaning: selector for child c of parent p

children.title: Flattened Disjunction Systems
children.top_down_role: Single-level representations of hierarchical logical structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Flattened Disjunction Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite nested disjunctions converted into an equivalent single-level family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the feasible set be described by a finite rooted tree whose internal nodes are unions and whose leaves are sets \(S_\ell\subseteq\mathbb R^n\). For each root-to-leaf selection \(p\) consistent with every encountered disjunction, let \(F_p\) be the intersection of the leaf and all constraints inherited along \(p\). The flattened system is
\[x\in\bigcup_{p\in\mathcal P}F_p.\]
It represents exactly the original nested system. If successive independent levels have \(m_1,\ldots,m_d\) alternatives, then \(|\mathcal P|=\prod_{k=1}^d m_k\), before removing infeasible or duplicate alternatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Flattening enumerates every consistent root-to-leaf choice and forms one top-level union of the resulting intersections, preserving feasibility but potentially multiplying alternatives.
assumptions_latex: Every constraint inherited along a selected path is conjoined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_{\mathrm{nested}}=\bigcup_{p\in\mathcal P}F_p\).

notation.meaning: Feasible set induced by selection p.

children.title: Index-Generated Disjunction Families
children.top_down_role: Alternative families generated from indexed or quantified relations.

children.title: Indexed Disjunctions
children.top_down_role: Alternative families generated over explicit index sets.

knowledge_statements.title: Indexed Disjunctions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A family of alternatives labeled by a common index set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be a set, let \(I\) be an index set, and let \(S_i\subseteq X\) for every \(i\in I\). For \(x\in X\), the indexed disjunction is the predicate
\[\bigvee_{i\in I}[x\in S_i],\]
whose feasible set is \(\bigcup_{i\in I}S_i\). The index labels alternatives and need not be a decision variable. Ordinary membership in the union requires at least one alternative to hold; a model requiring exactly one selected alternative must impose that additional logical condition separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An indexed disjunction requires a point to satisfy at least one member of a family of alternative sets labeled by a common index set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\text{ satisfies the disjunction}\iff x\in\bigcup_{i\in I}S_i\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Indexed linear disjunction over a feasible set
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines indexed disjunctive terms, validity over the feasible set, and the exceptional tautological form of the stated spatial disjunction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq\mathbb Z^r\times\mathbb R^{n-r}\) and define \(S_h=\{x\in S:A^h x\le b^h\}\), where \(A^h\in\mathbb Q^{m_h\times n}\), \(b^h\in\mathbb Q^{m_h}\), and \(h\in Q\). The indexed disjunction represents \(D=\bigcup_{h\in Q}S_h\). A point \(x\in S\) satisfies it when \(A^h x\le b^h\) for some \(h\in Q\); it is valid for all feasible solutions when \(S\subseteq D\). The extract calls the disjunction true when \(D\ne\varnothing\). The integer split \(x_i\le\alpha\vee x_i\ge\alpha+1\), with \(x_i\in\mathbb Z\) and \(\alpha\in\mathbb Z\), is valid. As written, the stated continuous disjunction \(x_i\le\beta\vee x_i\ge\beta\) covers every real value and is therefore tautological by itself.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An indexed disjunction is the union of indexed linear-inequality systems restricted to a feasible set. A feasible point satisfies it when it belongs to at least one term, and the disjunction is valid when every feasible point belongs to the union. The integer split is valid for integer variables. The continuous form printed in the extract is tautological and alone cannot strengthen a relaxation.
assumptions_latex: A^h\in\mathbb Q^{m_h\times n},\quad b^h\in\mathbb Q^{m_h}\quad(h\in Q)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D=\bigcup_{h\in Q}\{x\in S:A^h x\le b^h\},\qquad x\in D\iff\exists h\in Q:\ A^h x\le b^h.

children.title: Quantified Disjunctions
children.top_down_role: Alternative systems organized through quantified logical relations.

knowledge_statements.title: Quantified Disjunctions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Disjunction families generated within the scope of a universal quantifier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) and \(T\) be sets, let \(x\in X\), let \(I(t)\neq\varnothing\) index the alternatives available for each \(t\in T\), and let \(P(t,i,x)\) be a predicate defined for \(t\in T\), \(i\in I(t)\), and \(x\in X\). A universally quantified disjunction is
\[\forall t\in T,\quad \bigvee_{i\in I(t)}P(t,i,x).\]
It holds precisely when, for every \(t\in T\), there exists \(i\in I(t)\) for which \(P(t,i,x)\) holds. The witnessing index may depend on \(t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For every generated instance, at least one of its indexed alternatives must hold, and the witnessing alternative may vary with the instance.
assumptions_latex: \(P(t,i,x)\) is defined for \(t\in T\), \(i\in I(t)\), and \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall t\in T\;\bigvee_{i\in I(t)}P(t,i,x)\iff\forall t\in T\;\exists i\in I(t):P(t,i,x)\).

notation.meaning: Domain of the shared variable x.
Alternative indices available for instance t.
Predicate defining alternative i at instance t.

children.title: Finite Index Families
children.top_down_role: Disjunction systems generated from finite indexing structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Index Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary selection representation of a finite indexed disjunction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be a set, let \(I=\{1,\ldots,m\}\), and let \(S_i\subseteq X\) for every \(i\in I\). Introduce a binary selection indicator \(Y_i\) for each alternative and define
\[F=\left\{(x,Y)\in X\times\{0,1\}^m:Y_i=1\Rightarrow x\in S_i\ \text{for every }i\in I,\ \sum_{i\in I}Y_i\geq1\right\}.\]
Then \(\operatorname{proj}_x(F)=\bigcup_{i\in I}S_i\), provided every implication is represented exactly. If exactly one indicator must be selected, replace the inequality by \(\sum_{i\in I}Y_i=1\); this does not by itself make overlapping sets mutually exclusive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite disjunction can be represented using one binary selection indicator per alternative, exact indicator-to-alternative implications, and an at-least-one selection constraint. An exactly-one constraint governs the selected indicators, not membership in overlapping sets.
assumptions_latex: Each implication \(Y_i=1\Rightarrow x\in S_i\) is represented exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_x(F)=\bigcup_{i\in I}S_i\).

notation.meaning: Binary selection indicator for alternative i.
Feasible set of the extended logical representation.

children.title: Generated-Alternative Scope
children.top_down_role: Structural reach of indexed or quantified alternative generation.

knowledge_statements.title: Generated-Alternative Scope
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scoping rule for indices, variables, and constraints created by generation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the generated family \(\bigvee_{i\in I(t)}P(t,i,x,z_{t,i})\), the index \(i\) and local variable \(z_{t,i}\) are scoped only to alternative \((t,i)\), while \(x\) is shared across all alternatives. A well-scoped generation satisfies
\[\operatorname{fv}(P(t,i,x,z_{t,i}))\subseteq\{t,i,x,z_{t,i}\},\qquad z_{t,i}\cap z_{s,j}=\varnothing\ \text{for }(t,i)\neq(s,j),\]
unless an explicit linking equality identifies local variables. Consequently, constraints generated for an unselected alternative cannot silently restrict another alternative through an unintended shared local variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Generated alternatives share declared global variables but keep indices and local variables distinct unless explicit linking constraints identify them.
assumptions_latex: Every free index and variable has an enclosing declaration.
Local-variable copies are uniquely labeled by their generating indices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_{t,i}\cap z_{s,j}=\varnothing\) for distinct alternatives unless explicitly linked.

notation.meaning: Free variables and indices of predicate P.

children.title: Hierarchy-Flattening Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Structural loss and representation growth caused by flattening.

knowledge_statements.title: Hierarchy-Flattening Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact flattening may destroy factored structure and cause combinatorial representation growth.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each \(k\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\), let \(m_k\geq2\) and let \(S_{k,j}\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) for \(j\in\{1,\ldots,m_k\}\). Consider the factored feasible set
\[S=\bigcap_{k=1}^d\left(\bigcup_{j=1}^{m_k}S_{k,j}\right).\]
Exact flattening by distributivity gives
\[S=\bigcup_{(j_1,\ldots,j_d)\in\prod_{k=1}^d\{1,\ldots,m_k\}}\left(\bigcap_{k=1}^d S_{k,j_k}\right).\]
Before removing empty or duplicate intersections, the flat representation has \(N_{\mathrm{flat}}=\prod_{k=1}^d m_k\) alternatives, whereas the factored description lists \(\sum_{k=1}^d m_k\) alternatives across its levels. When \(m_k=2\) for every \(k\), the flat count is \(2^d\). Thus exact path enumeration can grow exponentially with depth while preserving the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a conjunction of independent levelwise disjunctions, distributing all choices into one union preserves feasibility but produces the product of the levelwise alternative counts, including 2^d alternatives in the binary case.
assumptions_latex: All Cartesian-product selections are enumerated before empty or duplicate intersections are removed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_{\mathrm{flat}}=\prod_{k=1}^d m_k\), and \(N_{\mathrm{flat}}=2^d\) when \(m_k=2\) for every \(k\).

notation.meaning: Alternative j in levelwise disjunction k.
Number of alternatives in levelwise disjunction k.
Number of enumerated flat alternatives before pruning.

children.title: Geometric Regimes of Disjunctions
children.top_down_role: Disjunctions distinguished by the geometry and ambient spaces of their alternatives.

children.title: Unions of Polyhedra
children.top_down_role: Linear alternatives represented in a common variable space.

knowledge_statements.title: Unions of Polyhedra
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite linear alternatives embedded in one Euclidean variable space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(i\in I=\{1,\ldots,m\}\), let
\[P_i=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:A_i x\leq b_i\}\]
be a polyhedron, allowing \(P_i\) to be empty or unbounded. A finite union of polyhedra is the generally nonconvex set
\[S=\bigcup_{i=1}^m P_i=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\bigvee_{i=1}^m[A_i x\leq b_i]\}.\]
All alternatives use the same ambient vector \(x\); differing row dimensions of \(A_i\) merely encode differing numbers of inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A union of polyhedra consists of points satisfying at least one of finitely many linear inequality systems in a common variable space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\bigvee_{i=1}^m[A_i x\leq b_i]\}\).

children.title: Unions of Convex Sets
children.top_down_role: Convex nonlinear alternatives and associated hull geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Unions of Convex Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite convex alternatives and the geometry of their union and hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty convex sets and let \(S=\bigcup_{i=1}^m C_i\). The union \(S\) need not be convex. Its convex hull is
\[\operatorname{conv}(S)=\left\{\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i x_i:\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m,\ \sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i=1,\ x_i\in C_i\right\}.\]
Zero-weight terms may use arbitrary points of their nonempty sets. Thus convexification permits simultaneous convex mixing across alternatives, whereas membership in \(S\) requires membership in at least one single alternative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A union of convex alternatives may be nonconvex; its convex hull contains all convex mixtures of points selected from those alternatives.
assumptions_latex: Each \(C_i\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_{i=1}^m C_i)=\{\sum_i\lambda_i x_i:\lambda\geq0,\ \sum_i\lambda_i=1,\ x_i\in C_i\}\).

notation.meaning: Convex-combination weight assigned to alternative i.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Reverse polar and elementary properties
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The final dimension-lineality identity is retained as extracted; its use of lineality as a numerical term is not fully explicit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), define \(S^\#:=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\langle x,y\rangle\ge 1\ \forall y\in S\}\). Then \(S^\#\) is convex; \((\lambda S)^\#=\lambda^{-1}S^\#\) for \(\lambda>0\); \(S\subseteq T\Rightarrow S^\#\supseteq T^\#\); \((S\cup T)^\#=S^\#\cap T^\#\); and polyhedrality of \(S\) implies polyhedrality of \(S^\#\). The extract additionally states \(\dim S^\#=n-\operatorname{lin}S^\#\), with \(\operatorname{lin}\) denoting lineality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The reverse polar of S consists of all vectors whose inner product with every point of S is at least one. It is convex, scales contravariantly under positive dilation, reverses inclusions, converts unions into intersections, and preserves polyhedrality. The extract also gives a dimension-lineality formula whose numerical notation is ambiguous.

children.title: Unions with Nonconvex Disjuncts
children.top_down_role: Alternatives requiring local or global convexification before union-level treatment.

knowledge_statements.title: Unions with Nonconvex Disjuncts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of disjunct-level convexification on the union and its global convex hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S_1,\ldots,S_m\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, possibly nonconvex sets. Replacing each alternative by its convex hull generally enlarges the disjunctive feasible set:
\[\bigcup_{i=1}^m S_i\subseteq\bigcup_{i=1}^m\operatorname{conv}(S_i),\]
and the inclusion may be strict. Nevertheless, global convexification commutes with this replacement:
\[\operatorname{conv}\left(\bigcup_{i=1}^m S_i\right)=\operatorname{conv}\left(\bigcup_{i=1}^m\operatorname{conv}(S_i)\right).\]
Thus disjunct-level convexification preserves the union's convex hull but not, in general, its original feasible points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convexifying each nonconvex alternative can add feasible points, although a subsequent global convex hull is unchanged.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_i S_i)=\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_i\operatorname{conv}(S_i))\).

children.title: Unbounded Disjuncts
children.top_down_role: Alternative sets containing unbounded feasible directions.

knowledge_statements.title: Unbounded Disjuncts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Alternatives containing rays and therefore lacking finite global coordinate bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A nonempty set \(C_i\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is an unbounded disjunct if, for every \(M>0\), there exists \(x\in C_i\) with \(\lVert x\rVert>M\). If \(C_i\) is closed and convex, this is equivalent to the existence of \(x^0\in C_i\) and a nonzero direction \(d\) such that
\[x^0+\alpha d\in C_i\qquad\text{for every }\alpha\geq0.\]
Such a direction belongs to the recession cone of \(C_i\), so formulations requiring finite bounds for every inactive alternative are not directly applicable without additional structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unbounded disjunct contains points of arbitrarily large norm; a closed convex one contains a ray in a nonzero recession direction.
assumptions_latex: The ray characterization assumes \(C_i\) is closed and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_i\text{ unbounded}\iff\operatorname{rec}(C_i)\neq\{0\}\) for nonempty closed convex \(C_i\).

children.title: Recession Cones
children.top_down_role: Directional geometry governing unbounded alternatives.

knowledge_statements.title: Recession Cones
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directions along which a closed convex disjunct extends indefinitely.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a nonempty closed convex set \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), its recession cone is
\[\operatorname{rec}(C)=\{d\in\mathbb R^n:x+\alpha d\in C\ \text{for every }x\in C\text{ and every }\alpha\geq0\}.\]
This set is a closed convex cone. Equivalently, it is enough to verify the ray condition from one fixed point \(x^0\in C\). If \(C=\{x:Ax\leq b\}\) is a nonempty polyhedron, then
\[\operatorname{rec}(C)=\{d:Ad\leq0\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The recession cone collects all directions that keep a closed convex set feasible under every nonnegative displacement.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rec}(C)\) is a closed convex cone, and \(\operatorname{rec}(C)=\{d:Ad\leq0\}\) for a nonempty polyhedron.

children.title: Common-Recession Regime
children.top_down_role: Union structures whose alternatives share compatible recession behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Common-Recession Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite convex alternatives sharing exactly the same asymptotic directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty closed convex sets. They are in the common-recession regime when there exists a closed convex cone \(K\) such that
\[\operatorname{rec}(C_i)=K\qquad\text{for every }i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}.\]
Equivalently, a direction \(d\) is a recession direction of one alternative if and only if it is a recession direction of every alternative. The bounded regime is the special case \(K=\{0\}\); any nonzero \(d\in K\) supplies a ray direction shared by all alternatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A family has common recession when every closed convex alternative admits exactly the same recession directions; bounded alternatives correspond to the zero cone.
assumptions_latex: Each \(C_i\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rec}(C_1)=\cdots=\operatorname{rec}(C_m)=K\).

children.title: Closure Failure Boundaries

knowledge_statements.title: Closure Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A concrete closure failure for the convex hull of closed convex disjuncts with incompatible recession geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_0=\{(0,0)\}\) and \(C_1=\{(u,v)\in\mathbb R^2:u>0,\ v\ge 1/u\}\). Both sets are closed and convex, but \(\operatorname{conv}(C_0\cup C_1)\) is not closed. Indeed, for every \(t>0\), the point \((t,0)\) is absent from this convex hull, whereas the sequence obtained using \(\lambda_k=1/k\) and \((u_k,v_k)=(kt,1/(kt))\in C_1\) satisfies \(\lambda_k(u_k,v_k)=(t,1/(k^2t))\to(t,0)\). Thus closure cannot generally be omitted when disjuncts have different recession behavior.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Closed convex disjuncts with incompatible recession behavior can have a nonclosed convex hull; the displayed two-set union gives an explicit example.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{conv}(C_0\cup C_1)\ne\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(C_0\cup C_1)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Unions in Heterogeneous Variable Spaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Common-space representation of alternatives whose native variables have different dimensions or meanings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each alternative \(i\in\{1,\ldots,k\}\), let \(C_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_i}\) be its local feasible set and let \(E_i:\mathbb R^{n_i}\to\mathbb R^N\) be a specified affine embedding into a common semantic space. The heterogeneous disjunction is represented by \[S=\bigcup_{i=1}^k E_i(C_i)=\{x\in\mathbb R^N:\exists i,\ \exists z_i\in C_i,\ x=E_i(z_i)\}.\] Convexification and comparison of alternatives are well-defined only after these embeddings, including conventions for absent coordinates, have been fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Embed each alternative’s native feasible set into one common coordinate space; the disjunction is the union of the embedded images.
assumptions_latex: Each \(E_i\) has a fixed interpretation for shared and absent coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S=\bigcup_{i=1}^k E_i(C_i)\subseteq\mathbb R^N\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex Hull Description for Two Upper-Monotone Polytopes in Different Spaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Here Z is the associated union set defined by the surrounding source construction; its definition is not repeated in this extract.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let M=\{1,\ldots,m\}, N=\{1,\ldots,n\}, P=\{x\in[0,1]^m:Ax\geq\mathbf 1\}, and Q=\{y\in[0,1]^n:By\geq\mathbf 1\}, where A=(a_{ij})\in\mathbb R_+^{p\times m} and B=(b_{k\ell})\in\mathbb R_+^{q\times n}. If P and Q are upper monotone, then \operatorname{conv}(Z) is the set of all (x,y)\in[0,1]^m\times[0,1]^n satisfying \[\sum_{j\in S}\frac{a_{ij}}{1-\sum_{h\in M\setminus S}a_{ih}}x_j+\sum_{\ell\in T}\frac{b_{k\ell}}{1-\sum_{h\in N\setminus T}b_{kh}}y_\ell\geq1\] for every i\in\{1,\ldots,p\}, k\in\{1,\ldots,q\}, S\subseteq M, and T\subseteq N such that \sum_{h\in M\setminus S}a_{ih}<1 and \sum_{h\in N\setminus T}b_{kh}<1.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For two upper-monotone polytopes in distinct coordinate spaces, each represented by a nonnegative covering system on a unit cube, the convex hull of the source-defined union Z consists exactly of the box-constrained pairs satisfying every admissible residual-normalized covering inequality.
assumptions_latex: A\in\mathbb R_+^{p\times m},\quad B\in\mathbb R_+^{q\times n}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{conv}(Z)=\left\{(x,y)\in[0,1]^m\times[0,1]^n:\sum_{j\in S}\frac{a_{ij}}{1-\sum_{h\in M\setminus S}a_{ih}}x_j+\sum_{\ell\in T}\frac{b_{k\ell}}{1-\sum_{h\in N\setminus T}b_{kh}}y_\ell\geq1\ \text{for every admissible }i,k,S,T\right\}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Aggregated and disaggregated plant-location formulations of set covering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compares integer equivalence and projected LP-relaxation strength for two auxiliary-variable formulations of a binary set-covering problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\{0,1\}^{M\times N}\), \(N_i=\{j\in N:a_{ij}=1\}\), and \(M_j=\{i\in M:a_{ij}=1\}\). The binary set-covering model \(\min\{c^\top x:Ax\ge e,\ x\in\{0,1\}^N\}\) is integer-equivalent to both the aggregated plant-location formulation \(\sum_{j\in N_i}u_{ij}\ge1\), \(\sum_{i\in M_j}u_{ij}\le |M_j|x_j\), and its disaggregated version \(\sum_{j\in N_i}u_{ij}\ge1\), \(u_{ij}\le x_j\). Projecting the aggregated LP relaxation gives \(\sum_{j\in N_S}|M_j|x_j\ge |S|\) for every \(S\subseteq M\), where \(N_S=\bigcup_{i\in S}N_i\); these inequalities are dominated by the corresponding sums of the set-covering inequalities, strictly when \(S\ne M\). Hence the aggregated relaxation is weaker than the set-covering LP relaxation. The disaggregated formulation projects to the original covering inequalities \(\sum_{j\in N_i}x_j\ge1\) and therefore has the same LP relaxation as the set-covering formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a binary set-covering model, both the aggregated and disaggregated uncapacitated plant-location formulations are equivalent at integer solutions. After relaxing integrality and projecting out the auxiliary variables, the aggregated formulation yields inequalities dominated by sums of the original covering inequalities, strictly for proper row subsets, so its LP relaxation is weaker. The disaggregated formulation recovers the original covering inequalities and has the same LP relaxation as set covering.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{proj}_x(P_{\mathrm{UPL}}^{LP})\supsetneq P_{\mathrm{SC}}^{LP}\ \text{in general},\qquad \operatorname{proj}_x(P_{\mathrm{UPL}'}^{LP})=P_{\mathrm{SC}}^{LP}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equivalent Tests for an Upper-Separation Parameter
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives seven equivalent conditions for the lower bound \(\alpha_P\ge\alpha\) in the upper-monotone setting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P\) be upper monotone of form (13.2) and let \(\alpha>0\). The following are equivalent:
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\text{(i) }\alpha_P\ge\alpha;\\
&\text{(ii) }\min_r\pi^r(x^*/\alpha)\ge1;\\
&\text{(iii) }x^*/\alpha\in P^+;\\
&\text{(iv) }\bigl(\min\{x_1^*/\alpha,1\},\ldots,\min\{x_n^*/\alpha,1\}\bigr)\in P;\\
&\text{(v) }\frac1\alpha\sum_{j\in S(\alpha)}a_jx_j^*+a\bigl(N\setminus S(\alpha)\bigr)\ge1;\\
&\text{(vi) }f(\alpha):=\sum_{j\in S(\alpha)}a_jx_j^*+\alpha a\bigl(N\setminus S(\alpha)\bigr)\ge\alpha;\\
&\text{(vii) }a\bigl(N\setminus S(\alpha)\bigr)\ge1\ \text{or}\ \bigl[a\bigl(N\setminus S(\alpha)\bigr)<1\ \text{and}\ g(\alpha)\ge\alpha\bigr].
\end{aligned}
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an upper-monotone P of form (13.2) and positive alpha, the bound alpha_P at least alpha is equivalent to the minimum separation-function test, scaled membership in the dominant, componentwise-truncated membership in P, two stated weighted-sum inequalities, and the stated alternative involving g(alpha).
assumptions_latex: P\text{ is upper monotone of form (13.2)}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Conditions (i)--(vii) in the displayed statement are equivalent.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Disjunction of Polytopes in Disjoint Variable Spaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the disjunctive set for polytopes in separate coordinate spaces. In the source context, P^* denotes the blocker of P.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given polytopes \(P\subseteq[0,1]^m\) and \(Q\subseteq[0,1]^n\), define
\[
Z=\{(x,y)\in[0,1]^m\times[0,1]^n:x\in P\ \text{or}\ y\in Q\}=(P\times[0,1]^n)\cup([0,1]^m\times Q).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For polytopes P and Q in separate unit-cube coordinate spaces, Z is the set of pairs (x,y) such that x belongs to P or y belongs to Q. Equivalently, it is the union of P times the full y-cube and the full x-cube times Q.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Z=\{(x,y)\in[0,1]^m\times[0,1]^n:x\in P\ \mathrm{or}\ y\in Q\}=(P\times[0,1]^n)\cup([0,1]^m\times Q)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closed Form for the Upper-Separation Parameter
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies the active index set and value of \(\alpha_P\) from a maximal eligible component of \(x^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(P\) is upper monotone of form (13.2), and let
\[
x_q^*=\max\left\{x_j^*:a\bigl(N\setminus S(x_j^*)\bigr)<1\ \text{and}\ x_j^*\le g(x_j^*)\right\}.
\]
Then
\[
S(\alpha_P)=S(x_q^*)
\quad\text{and}\quad
\alpha_P=\frac{\sum_{j\in S(x_q^*)}a_jx_j^*}{1-a\bigl(N\setminus S(x_q^*)\bigr)}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an upper-monotone P, let x_q* be the largest eligible component satisfying the stated conditions. The active set at alpha_P equals the active set at x_q*, and alpha_P is the displayed weighted-sum ratio.
assumptions_latex: P\text{ is upper monotone of form (13.2)}.
x_q^*=\max\{x_j^*:a(N\setminus S(x_j^*))<1,\ x_j^*\le g(x_j^*)\}\text{ is defined}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex-hull representation for a union in heterogeneous binary-variable spaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded characterization relying on the chapter's prior definitions of Z, P^S, Q^T, and their indexed valid inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(S\subseteq M\), let
\[
\sum_{j\in S_r^+}\pi_j^r x_j+\sum_{j\in S_r^-}\pi_j^r(1-x_j)\ge 1,\qquad r\in V^S,
\]
be the valid inequalities of \(P^S\) that define faces of dimension \(|S|-1\) and have full support, meaning \(\pi_j^r>0\) for every \(j\in S\) and \((S_r^+,S_r^-)\) partitions \(S\). Define \(\mu^s,T_s^+,T_s^-\) analogously for \(Q^T\), for every \(T\subseteq N\) and \(s\in V^T\). Then
\[
\operatorname{conv}(Z)=\left\{(x,y)\in[0,1]^m\times[0,1]^n:\begin{aligned}&\sum_{j\in S_r^+}\pi_j^r x_j+\sum_{j\in S_r^-}\pi_j^r(1-x_j)\\&+\sum_{j\in T_s^+}\mu_j^s y_j+\sum_{j\in T_s^-}\mu_j^s(1-y_j)\ge1
e\end{aligned}\ \text{for all }r\in\bigcup_{S\subseteq M}V^S,\ s\in\bigcup_{T\subseteq N}V^T\right\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For every subset of each variable-index set, consider the full-support valid inequalities of the associated polytopes that define faces of the stated codimension. The convex hull of Z is exactly the set of points in the product of the two unit cubes satisfying every inequality formed by adding one indexed P-side expression and one indexed Q-side expression and requiring their sum to be at least one.
assumptions_latex: \sum_{j\in S_r^+}\pi_j^r x_j+\sum_{j\in S_r^-}\pi_j^r(1-x_j)\ge1\text{ is valid for }P^S\text{ and defines a face of dimension }|S|-1
\mu^s,T_s^+,T_s^-\text{ are defined analogously from the corresponding full-support inequalities of }Q^T
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{conv}(Z)=\left\{(x,y)\in[0,1]^m\times[0,1]^n:\sum_{j\in S_r^+}\pi_j^r x_j+\sum_{j\in S_r^-}\pi_j^r(1-x_j)+\sum_{j\in T_s^+}\mu_j^s y_j+\sum_{j\in T_s^-}\mu_j^s(1-y_j)\ge1\ \forall r\in\bigcup_{S\subseteq M}V^S,\ \forall s\in\bigcup_{T\subseteq N}V^T\right\}

knowledge_statements.title: Disaggregated-Variable Hull Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact lifted hull formulation for a finite union of nonempty polytopes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_i=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:A_i x\le b_i\}\) be nonempty polytopes for \(i=1,\ldots,k\). Then \(\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_i P_i)\) is the projection onto \(x\) of \[x=\sum_{i=1}^k v_i,\qquad A_i v_i\le b_i\lambda_i\ \ (i=1,\ldots,k),\qquad \sum_{i=1}^k\lambda_i=1,\qquad \lambda_i\ge0.\] Here \(v_i\) is the contribution local to alternative \(i\). For \(\lambda_i>0\), \(v_i/\lambda_i\in P_i\); boundedness ensures that \(\lambda_i=0\) forces \(v_i=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A union-of-polytopes hull is obtained by scaling one local variable copy per alternative, summing those copies, and projecting away the local variables and weights.
assumptions_latex: Each \(P_i=\{x:A_i x\le b_i\}\) is a nonempty polytope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)=\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_{i=1}^kP_i)\), where \(Q\) is the displayed lifted system.

notation.meaning: disaggregated variable contribution for alternative i

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Disaggregated extended formulation for a finite disjunctive hull
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex-hull representation for a finite union of bounded polyhedral alternatives using alternative-local variable copies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let P_i=\{y:A_i y\le b_i,\ 0\le y\le u_i\} for i=1,\ldots,k, and encode selection of exactly one alternative by x\in\{0,1\}^k with \sum_{i=1}^k x_i=1. The convex hull of the resulting feasible (x,y)-pairs is the projection of the extended system
\[
y=\sum_{i=1}^k y_i,\qquad A_i y_i\le b_i x_i,\qquad 0\le y_i\le u_i x_i\quad(i=1,\ldots,k),
\]
\[
\sum_{i=1}^k x_i=1,\qquad x\in[0,1]^k.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For finitely many bounded polyhedral alternatives, introduce one local copy of the continuous variable for each alternative and scale that alternative's constraints and bounds by its selection variable. Requiring the local copies to sum to the original variable, the selection variables to sum to one, and relaxing those variables to the unit cube gives an extended formulation whose projection is the convex hull of the disjunctive feasible pairs.
assumptions_latex: P_i=\{y:A_i y\le b_i,\ 0\le y\le u_i\},\quad i=1,\ldots,k
x\in\{0,1\}^k,\quad \sum_{i=1}^k x_i=1\text{ in the original disjunctive model}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{conv}(S)=\operatorname{proj}_{x,y}\left\{(x,y,y_1,\ldots,y_k):y=\sum_{i=1}^k y_i,\ A_i y_i\le b_i x_i,\ 0\le y_i\le u_i x_i,\ \sum_{i=1}^k x_i=1,\ x\in[0,1]^k\right\}.

knowledge_statements.title: Projection Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the interface between a lifted feasible set and its represented original-space set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+q}\) have coordinates \((x,y)\), and let \(\pi_x(x,y)=x\). The projection interface of \(Q\) is the existentially quantified set \[P=\pi_x(Q)=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\exists y\in\mathbb R^q\text{ with }(x,y)\in Q\}.\] An extended formulation is exact for a target set \(T\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) precisely when \(\pi_x(Q)=T\); it is an outer formulation when \(T\subseteq\pi_x(Q)\), and an inner formulation when \(\pi_x(Q)\subseteq T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection removes auxiliary coordinates existentially. Exactness means that the resulting original-space set equals the intended target.
assumptions_latex: The original and auxiliary coordinate blocks are fixed as \(x\) and \(y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P=\{x:\exists y,\ (x,y)\in Q\}\).

notation.meaning: coordinate projection onto the original variables

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Extreme-ray representation of a polyhedral projection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines coordinate projection and gives its inequality description through extreme rays of a nonnegative multiplier cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
S:=\{(x,u)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^p:Ax+Bu\le b\},
\]
where \(A\), \(B\), and \(b\) have \(m\) rows, and define
\[
\operatorname{Proj}_x(S):=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\exists u\in\mathbb R^p\text{ such that }(x,u)\in S\}.
\]
For
\[
W:=\{v\in\mathbb R^m:vB=0,\ v\ge0\},
\]
we have
\[
\operatorname{Proj}_x(S)=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:(vA)x\le vb\ \forall v\in\operatorname{extr}W\},
\]
where \(\operatorname{extr}W\) denotes the extreme rays of \(W\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The projection consists of the original-space points admitting feasible auxiliary variables. Equivalently, it is described by the inequalities generated by extreme rays of the nonnegative multiplier cone that annihilates the auxiliary-variable matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Proj}_x(S)=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:(vA)x\le vb\ \forall v\in\operatorname{extr}W\}.

knowledge_statements.title: Lifted-Variable Elimination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fourier–Motzkin elimination for one auxiliary variable in a finite linear lifted description.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R\) be a finite index set, let \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(y\in\mathbb R\), and consider the inequalities \(a_r^\top x+\alpha_r y\le b_r\) for \(r\in R\), where \(a_r\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(\alpha_r,b_r\in\mathbb R\). Partition \(R\) into \(I^+=\{r\in R:\alpha_r>0\}\), \(I^-=\{r\in R:\alpha_r<0\}\), and \(I^0=\{r\in R:\alpha_r=0\}\). Retain every inequality indexed by \(I^0\). For each \((p,m)\in I^+\times I^-\), add the inequality obtained from the nonnegative combination \[(-\alpha_m)(a_p^\top x+\alpha_p y)+(\alpha_p)(a_m^\top x+\alpha_m y)\le(-\alpha_m)b_p+\alpha_p b_m,\] in which \(y\) cancels. The resulting system in \(x\) describes the projection onto the \(x\)-coordinates. Repeat the procedure for additional real auxiliary variables, optionally removing redundant inequalities after each step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite linear system, Fourier–Motzkin elimination pairs inequalities having positive and negative coefficients on a real auxiliary variable, cancels that variable, and retains inequalities having zero coefficient.
assumptions_latex: \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), \(y\in\mathbb R\), \(a_r\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(\alpha_r,b_r\in\mathbb R\) for every \(r\in R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The generated inequalities define \(\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\exists y\in\mathbb R,\ a_r^\top x+\alpha_r y\le b_r\ \text{for every }r\in R\}\).

notation.meaning: finite index set of input inequalities
positive-, negative-, and zero-coefficient index classes

knowledge_statements.title: Original-Space Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility and objective recovery through an exact coordinate projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+q}\) be an exact extension of \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), so \(P=\pi_x(Q)\). Then \(x\in P\) if and only if there exists \(y\in\mathbb R^q\) with \((x,y)\in Q\). Moreover, for every objective vector \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \[\inf_{x\in P}c^Tx=\inf_{(x,y)\in Q}c^Tx.\] Whenever the lifted problem attains an optimizer \((x^*,y^*)\), its original component \(x^*\) is feasible for \(P\) and is optimal for the original-space problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact extension recovers original feasibility existentially and preserves every objective depending only on original variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in P\iff\exists y:(x,y)\in Q\), and \(\inf_{x\in P}c^Tx=\inf_{(x,y)\in Q}c^Tx\).

knowledge_statements.title: Elimination Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case inequality proliferation under unreduced Fourier–Motzkin elimination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a linear system initially has \(m\ge2\) inequalities and \(q\) real auxiliary variables are eliminated successively by Fourier–Motzkin elimination without redundancy removal. If \(m_j\) denotes the number of inequalities after \(j\) eliminations, then one elimination generates at most one inequality per positive-negative pair plus the zero-coefficient inequalities, so \(m_{j+1}\le m_j^2+m_j\le2m_j^2\). Consequently, \[m_q\le 2^{2^q-1}m^{2^q}.\] Thus direct symbolic elimination has a doubly exponential worst-case output bound in the number of eliminated variables, even before redundancy testing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without redundancy removal, successive Fourier–Motzkin elimination can produce doubly exponentially many inequalities in the number of eliminated variables.
assumptions_latex: The initial system has \(m\ge2\) linear inequalities.
No generated inequality is removed as redundant.

notation.meaning: inequality count after j elimination steps

children.title: Minimal Lifted Descriptions

knowledge_statements.title: Minimal Lifted Descriptions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimality relative to a fixed original-variable block and a specified class of linear extensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), and let \(Q=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^{n+q}:A x+B y\le d\}\) satisfy \(\pi_x(Q)=P\). Relative to a class \(\mathcal E\) of admissible linear extensions, call this description minimal if its size pair \((q,m)\), where \(m\) is the number of inequalities, is lexicographically minimal among members of \(\mathcal E\) projecting to \(P\), after equations and implied equalities are treated according to a fixed convention. It is inequality-irredundant if deleting any displayed inequality strictly enlarges \(Q\) or changes its projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lifted description is minimal within a fixed extension class when auxiliary dimension and then inequality count cannot be reduced; irredundancy forbids removable inequalities.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal E\) fixes the permitted extension class and counting convention.
Every compared extension retains the same original coordinate block \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((q,m)=\min_{\mathrm{lex}}\{(q',m'):Q'\in\mathcal E,\ \pi_x(Q')=P\}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniqueness of an Irredundant Relative-Affine Polyhedral Description

children.title: Facet-Projection Geometry

knowledge_statements.title: Facet-Projection Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exposed faces under linear projection and the criterion for their projected image to be a facet.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+q}\) be a polytope, let \(P=\pi_x(Q)\), and let \(c\in\mathbb R^n\). Define \(F_Q(c)=\operatorname*{argmax}_{(x,y)\in Q}c^Tx\) and \(F_P(c)=\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in P}c^Tx\). Then \[\pi_x(F_Q(c))=F_P(c).\] Hence the lifted exposed face associated with the pulled-back normal \((c,0)\) projects to a facet of \(P\) exactly when \(\dim F_P(c)=\dim P-1\). A facet of \(Q\) need not project to a facet, because projection may lower its dimension or map it onto all of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A projected exposed face equals the exposed face of the projection for the same original-space objective; it is a facet exactly under the usual dimension test.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\pi_x(F_Q(c))=F_P(c)\), with facet status iff \(\dim F_P(c)=\dim P-1\).

notation.meaning: exposed face of Q for objective c on original coordinates
corresponding exposed face of the projection

knowledge_statements.title: Polar Descriptions of Union Hulls
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polar identity for the closed convex hull of a finite union containing the origin.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_1,\ldots,C_k\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty sets containing \(0\), and define their polars by \(C_i^\circ=\{a\in\mathbb R^n:a^Tx\le1\ \forall x\in C_i\}\). If \(H=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_{i=1}^k C_i)\), then \[H^\circ=\bigcap_{i=1}^k C_i^\circ.\] Consequently, a normalized inequality \(a^Tx\le1\) is valid for the union hull exactly when it is valid for every disjunct. Since \(H\) is closed, convex, and contains \(0\), bipolarity also gives \(H=(\bigcap_i C_i^\circ)^\circ\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The polar of a closed union hull is the intersection of the disjunct polars, so valid normalized inequalities are precisely their common polar vectors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H^\circ=\bigcap_iC_i^\circ\) and \(H=(\bigcap_iC_i^\circ)^\circ\).

notation.meaning: polar set under unit right-hand-side normalization
closed convex hull of the union

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Scaled polar and its disjunctive representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The multiplier representation relies on the hypotheses of the referenced disjunctive Farkas lemma, which are not restated in this extract.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and \(\alpha_0\in\mathbb R\), define \[F_{(\alpha_0)}^\#:=\{y\in\mathbb R^n:\langle x,y\rangle\ge\alpha_0\ \forall x\in F\}.\] After positive normalization of a nonzero threshold, the relevant signs are \(\alpha_0=1\) and \(\alpha_0=-1\), while zero remains \(0\). Thus \(F_{(1)}^\#=F^\#\), \(F_{(-1)}^\#=-F^0\), and, for a cone \(C\), \(C_{(0)}^\#=-C^0\). If \(\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}F=\operatorname{conv}\{v^1,\ldots,v^p\}+\operatorname{cone}\{w^1,\ldots,w^q\}\), then \[F_{(\alpha_0)}^\#=\{y:(v^i)^Ty\ge\alpha_0\ (i=1,\ldots,p),\ (w^j)^Ty\ge0\ (j=1,\ldots,q)\}.\] Under the referenced disjunctive Farkas-lemma hypotheses for alternatives \(A^h x\ge b^h\), membership is equivalently certified by multipliers \(u^h\ge0\) satisfying \(y=u^hA^h\) and \(u^hb^h\ge\alpha_0\) for every alternative \(h\); the pairs \((y,\alpha_0)\) are consequently a projection of that multiplier system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The scaled polar is the family of normals defining inequalities with common right-hand side alpha-zero that are valid on F. Its normalized positive, negative, and zero cases recover the reverse polar, the negative ordinary polar, and, for cones, the negative polar cone. It also admits extreme-generator and, under the referenced disjunctive Farkas assumptions, multiplier and projection descriptions.
assumptions_latex: F\text{ is represented by the stated disjunctive linear alternatives and satisfies the hypotheses of the referenced disjunctive Farkas lemma for the multiplier representation}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F_{(\alpha_0)}^\#=\{y:\langle x,y\rangle\ge\alpha_0\ \forall x\in F\},\quad F_{(1)}^\#=F^\#,\quad F_{(-1)}^\#=-F^0

knowledge_statements.title: Blocking Union Hulls
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Blocking-set closure under union convexification and its blocker-intersection identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonempty closed convex blocking sets \(P_i\subseteq\mathbb R_+^n\), meaning \(P_i+\mathbb R_+^n=P_i\), define \(H=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_{i=1}^kP_i)\) and the blocker \(B(P)=\{y\in\mathbb R_+^n:y^Tx\ge1\ \forall x\in P\}\). Then \(H\) is blocking and \[B(H)=\bigcap_{i=1}^kB(P_i).\] Thus a nonnegative blocking inequality \(y^Tx\ge1\) is valid for the blocking union hull exactly when it is valid for every disjunct.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The closed convex hull of blocking disjuncts remains blocking, and its blocker is the intersection of the individual blockers.
assumptions_latex: Each \(P_i\subseteq\mathbb R_+^n\) is nonempty, closed, convex, and blocking.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H+\mathbb R_+^n=H\) and \(B(H)=\bigcap_iB(P_i)\).

notation.meaning: closed convex hull of the blocking union

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: universal validity over a union yields intersection of blockers

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The blocking-closure and blocker-intersection claims are coherent and appropriately classified as duality, but they lack an inspectable authoritative citation.

children.title: Monotone Union Hulls
children.top_down_role: Convex hull structures associated with monotone alternatives.

knowledge_statements.title: Monotone Union Hulls
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Preservation of coordinatewise upper monotonicity by union, convexification, and closure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_1,\ldots,C_k\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be upper monotone under the componentwise order: whenever \(x\in C_i\) and \(d\in\mathbb R_+^n\), one has \(x+d\in C_i\). Then the union \(U=\bigcup_iC_i\), its convex hull, and its closed convex hull are upper monotone. Equivalently, \[\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(U)+\mathbb R_+^n=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(U).\] If every \(C_i\subseteq\mathbb R_+^n\), the resulting closed union hull is therefore a blocking set under the upward-closed convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coordinatewise upward closure is preserved by finite union, convexification, and topological closure, yielding a monotone union hull.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_iC_i)+\mathbb R_+^n=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_iC_i)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: upper comprehensiveness is preserved by union, convex hull, and closure

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Preservation of upper monotonicity is correct, but the classification as a blocking set normally also requires nonemptiness, which is not assumed. No authoritative locator is supplied to settle the intended convention.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Alpha-Sum Membership Criterion for an Upper-Monotone Union Hull
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Membership characterization using the quantities α_P and α_Q from the associated upper-monotone union construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If P and Q are upper monotone and (x^*,y^*)\in[0,1]^m\times[0,1]^n, then \[(x^*,y^*)\in\operatorname{conv}(Z)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \alpha_P+\alpha_Q\geq1.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For upper-monotone P and Q, a box-constrained point belongs to the convex hull of the associated union Z if and only if its two associated alpha quantities have sum at least one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (x^*,y^*)\in\operatorname{conv}(Z)\iff\alpha_P+\alpha_Q\geq1

knowledge_statements.title: Dominant-Set Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed convex dominant generated by a nonnegative set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonempty set \(S\subseteq\mathbb{R}_+^n\), its dominant is \[\operatorname{domn}(S):=\operatorname{cl}\!\left(\operatorname{conv}(S)+\mathbb{R}_+^n\right).\] A set \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}_+^n\) is a closed convex dominant set precisely when it is nonempty, closed, convex, and satisfies \(P+\mathbb{R}_+^n=P\). Consequently, membership is monotone: if \(x\in P\) and \(y\geq x\) componentwise, then \(y\in P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dominant is the closed convex hull of a nonnegative set plus the nonnegative orthant; it contains every point componentwise above any of its members.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{domn}(S)+\mathbb{R}_+^n=\operatorname{domn}(S)\).

notation.meaning: closed convex dominant generated by S

knowledge_statements.title: Polarity Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Blocking polarity for closed convex dominant subsets of \(\mathbb{R}_+^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}_+^n\), define its blocker by \[\mathcal{B}(P):=\{y\in\mathbb{R}_+^n:y^{\mathsf T}x\geq1\ \text{for every }x\in P\}.\] If \(P\) is a nonempty closed convex dominant, \(0\notin P\), and \(\mathcal{B}(P)\neq\varnothing\), then \(\mathcal{B}(P)\) is also a closed convex dominant and blocking polarity is involutive: \[\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{B}(P))=P.\] Thus inequalities indexed by one dominant provide a polarity interface to the points of its blocker.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Blocking polarity maps a suitable closed convex dominant to all nonnegative vectors giving valid level-one inequalities, and applying the operation twice recovers the original dominant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{B}(P))=P\).

knowledge_statements.title: Closed Perspective Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower-semicontinuous perspective of a proper closed convex function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper, closed, and convex. Its closed perspective is \[f^{\pi}(x,t):=\begin{cases}t f(x/t),&t>0,\\ f^{\infty}(x),&t=0,\\ +\infty,&t<0,\end{cases}\] where \(f^{\infty}\) is the recession function of \(f\). The function \(f^{\pi}\) is closed, convex, and positively homogeneous. For an activation variable \(t\in\{0,1\}\), the epigraph constraint \(r\geq f^{\pi}(x,t)\) models the active epigraph at \(t=1\) and its recession-compatible closure at \(t=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The closed perspective uses the scaled function for positive activation and the recession function at zero, producing a closed convex activated epigraph.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f^{\pi}\) is closed, convex, and positively homogeneous on \(\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Conic Perspective Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Homogenized conic lift of a closed perspective epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(K\) is a closed convex cone and \[\operatorname{epi}f=\{(x,r):\exists u,\ Ax+Br+Cu+d\in K\}.\] The homogenized conic set \[H:=\{(x,t,r):t\geq0,\ \exists v,\ Ax+Br+Cv+dt\in K\}\] is convex and positively homogeneous. If \(H\) is closed and the displayed lift is exact under homogenization, then \(H=\operatorname{epi}f^{\pi}\). Without closedness of the projection, the universally valid relation is \(\operatorname{epi}f^{\pi}=\operatorname{cl}H\). Thus activation is represented by multiplying only the affine offset by \(t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conic epigraph lift is perspectivized by homogenizing its affine offset; closure of the projected cone may be required at zero activation.
assumptions_latex: \(\operatorname{epi}f\) has the stated exact conic lift.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{epi}f^{\pi}=\operatorname{cl}H\), and equality with \(H\) holds when \(H\) is closed.

children.title: Perspective Domains
children.top_down_role: Domain structure governing perspective convexification.

knowledge_statements.title: Perspective Domains
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effective domain of the closed perspective, including its zero slice.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a proper closed convex function \(f\), the effective domain of its closed perspective satisfies \[\operatorname{dom}f^{\pi}=\{(x,t):t>0,\ x/t\in\operatorname{dom}f\}\ \cup\ \{(x,0):f^{\infty}(x)<+\infty\}.\] No point with \(t<0\) belongs to the domain. Equivalently, the positive slice at \(t\) is \(t\operatorname{dom}f\), while the zero slice is the effective domain of the recession function.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive perspective slices scale the original domain; the zero slice consists exactly of directions where the recession function is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dom}f^{\pi}=\{(x,t):t>0,\ x\in t\operatorname{dom}f\}\cup\{(x,0):x\in\operatorname{dom}f^{\infty}\}\).

children.title: Inactive-State Closure
children.top_down_role: Closure behavior at the inactive state.

knowledge_statements.title: Inactive-State Closure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recession epigraph supplied by closure at zero activation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) be proper, closed, and convex. The inactive slice of the closed perspective epigraph is \[\{(x,r):(x,0,r)\in\operatorname{epi}f^{\pi}\}=\operatorname{epi}f^{\infty}.\] In particular, if \(f^{\infty}(x)=+\infty\) for every \(x\neq0\), then zero activation forces \(x=0\), with \(r\geq f^{\infty}(0)=0\). More generally, nonzero inactive values are permitted exactly along recession directions having finite recession cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At zero activation, the closed perspective retains precisely the recession epigraph; only finite-cost recession directions can remain nonzero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{(x,r):(x,0,r)\in\operatorname{epi}f^{\pi}\}=\operatorname{epi}f^{\infty}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Boundary Extensions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unique lower-semicontinuous extension of the positive perspective to \(t=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(g(x,t)=t f(x/t)\) for \(t>0\), where \(f\) is proper, closed, and convex. Its lower-semicontinuous convex extension to \(t\geq0\) is characterized at the boundary by \[g(x,0)=f^{\infty}(x)=\sup_{z\in\operatorname{dom}f}\bigl(f(z+x)-f(z)\bigr).\] Equivalently, \(\operatorname{epi}g\) is the closure of the positive-scale epigraph. This boundary assignment is the unique closed, convex, positively homogeneous extension agreeing with \(t f(x/t)\) for every \(t>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Closing the positive perspective assigns the recession value at zero, yielding the unique closed convex positively homogeneous extension.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g(x,0)=f^{\infty}(x)\) and \(\operatorname{epi}g=\operatorname{cl}\{(x,t,r):t>0,\ r\geq t f(x/t)\}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Nonclosed Perspective Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure caused by omitting the zero-activation boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Take \(f(x)=x^2\) on \(\mathbb{R}\) and define the unextended perspective \[q(x,t)=\begin{cases}x^2/t,&t>0,\\ +\infty,&t\leq0.\end{cases}\] Then \(q\) is convex on its effective domain but is not lower semicontinuous on \(\mathbb{R}^2\): the epigraph points \((0,1/k,0)\) converge to \((0,0,0)\), which is absent from \(\operatorname{epi}q\). Its closed perspective adds the boundary value \(q^{\mathrm{cl}}(0,0)=0\) and assigns \(q^{\mathrm{cl}}(x,0)=+\infty\) for \(x\neq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The raw quadratic perspective excluding zero activation has a nonclosed epigraph; closure adds the missing origin at the inactive boundary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{epi}q\) is not closed, whereas \(\operatorname{cl}(\operatorname{epi}q)=\operatorname{epi}q^{\mathrm{cl}}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sequential Convexification Theorem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact progressive convexification of designated binary coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I=\{1,\ldots,p\}\) and let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a polyhedron satisfying \(0\le x_j\le1\) for every \(j\in I\). If \((P)^t\) denotes sequential convexification through the first \(t\) binary-coordinate disjunctions, then for every \(t\in\{1,\ldots,p\}\), \[(P)^t=\operatorname{conv}\{x\in P:x_j\in\{0,1\}\text{ for }j=1,\ldots,t\}.\] Consequently, for \(S=\{x\in P:x_j\in\{0,1\}\text{ for }j\in I\}\), one has \((P)^p=\operatorname{conv}(S)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After sequentially convexifying the first t binary-coordinate disjunctions, the resulting set is exactly the convex hull of points of P integral in those t coordinates. Processing all p coordinates yields the mixed-binary hull.
assumptions_latex: P\subseteq\{x\in\mathbb R^n:0\le x_j\le1\ \forall j\in I\}\text{ is a polyhedron}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (P)^t=\operatorname{conv}\{x\in P:x_j\in\{0,1\},\ j=1,\ldots,t\},\qquad (P)^p=\operatorname{conv}(S).

children.title: Basic-Step Convexification

knowledge_statements.title: Basic-Step Convexification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One local distributive combination followed by convexification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a relaxation \(R\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) and two finite disjunctions \(D^p=\bigcup_{i\in I}P_i\) and \(D^q=\bigcup_{j\in J}Q_j\). Form their combined disjunction \[D^{pq}:=\bigcup_{(i,j)\in I\times J}(P_i\cap Q_j),\] and update \[R^+:=R\cap\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(D^{pq}).\] Leave all unselected disjunctions unchanged. A sequential procedure repeats this basic step for selected pairs and stops after the prescribed sequence or when no selected update changes the current relaxation; its output is the final \(R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A basic step combines two selected disjunctions by distributing their terms, convexifies the resulting union, and intersects that hull with the current relaxation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R^+=R\cap\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}\bigl(\bigcup_{i,j}(P_i\cap Q_j)\bigr)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Constraint-Boundary Characterization of a Sequential Convexification Step
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary-and-sufficient boundary criterion for the stage-j inclusion described by condition (3.5); the boundary is relative to the affine space spanned by $\bar D_j$.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
In the sequential-convexification setting, let $[x,y]$ denote the segment joining $x$ and $y$, and take $\operatorname{bd}\bar D_j$ relative to $\operatorname{aff}(\bar D_j)$. Then
\[
(\operatorname{conv}F_{j-1})\cap D_j\subseteq \operatorname{conv}(F_{j-1}\cap D_j)
\]
if and only if
\[
\forall x\in F_{j-1}\cap\bar D_j\;\forall y\in F_{j-1}\cap D_j:\quad [x,y]\cap\operatorname{bd}\bar D_j\subseteq \operatorname{conv}(F_{j-1}\cap D_j).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The stage-j inclusion holds exactly when every boundary point lying on a segment from the $\bar D_j$ portion of the current set to its $D_j$ portion belongs to the convex hull of the latter portion.
assumptions_latex: F_{j-1},D_j,\bar D_j\text{ are the stage-}j\text{ sets from the sequential-convexification setting}
\operatorname{bd}\bar D_j\text{ is taken relative to }\operatorname{aff}(\bar D_j)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (\operatorname{conv}F_{j-1})\cap D_j\subseteq\operatorname{conv}(F_{j-1}\cap D_j)\iff \forall x\in F_{j-1}\cap\bar D_j\;\forall y\in F_{j-1}\cap D_j:\ [x,y]\cap\operatorname{bd}\bar D_j\subseteq\operatorname{conv}(F_{j-1}\cap D_j)

children.title: Faciality Criteria
children.top_down_role: Facial structure relevant to sequential convexification.

knowledge_statements.title: Faciality Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A stagewise face condition for disjunctive terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_k\) be the closed convex relaxation before stage \(k\), and let the selected disjunction have terms \(P_{k,i}\). The stage satisfies the faciality criterion when, for every \(i\), either \(R_k\cap P_{k,i}=\varnothing\) or there exists a valid inequality \(a_{k,i}^{\mathsf T}x\leq\beta_{k,i}\) for \(R_k\) such that \[R_k\cap P_{k,i}=\{x\in R_k:a_{k,i}^{\mathsf T}x=\beta_{k,i}\}.\] Hence every nonempty selected term cuts out an exposed face of the current relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The faciality criterion requires each nonempty selected disjunctive term to coincide with an exposed face of the current convex relaxation.
assumptions_latex: \(\{P_{k,i}\}_{i\in I_k}\) is a finite selected disjunction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_k\cap P_{k,i}\) is empty or an exposed face of \(R_k\) for every \(i\in I_k\).

notation.meaning: term i of the selected disjunction

knowledge_statements.title: Sequential Convexifiability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite attainment by an ordered sequence of basic steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A formulation is sequentially convexifiable when finitely many admissible basic steps, in some order, produce exactly the closed convex hull of the disjunctive set.
assumptions_latex: Each \(T_{\nu_k}\) is an admissible basic-step convexification operator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_m=\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(S)\) for some finite admissible sequence.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Full Sequential Convexification of a Mixed 0-1 Set
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded mixed 0-1 specialization of finite sequential hull recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
K^0:=K\cap\{x\in\mathbb R^n:x_j\in\{0,1\},\ j=1,\ldots,p\}.
\]
After sequential convexification with respect to all p designated coordinates,
\[
P_{1,\ldots,p}(K)=\operatorname{conv}(K^0).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sequentially convexifying every designated binary coordinate recovers the convex hull of the mixed 0-1 points of K.
assumptions_latex: P_{1,\ldots,p}(K)\text{ is obtained by sequential convexification with respect to all }p\text{ designated coordinates}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P_{1,\ldots,p}(K)=\operatorname{conv}(K^0).

children.title: Criterion Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Geometric cases where sequential recovery criteria do not hold.

knowledge_statements.title: Criterion Failure Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure is defined relative to a specified sequence of partial-convexification operators and its intended union hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U=\bigcup_{i=1}^m S_i\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(H=\operatorname{conv}(U)\), and let \(R_0\supseteq U\). For operators \(T_1,\ldots,T_k\) satisfying \(U\subseteq T_j(R)\subseteq R\) whenever \(U\subseteq R\), define \(R_j=T_j(R_{j-1})\). A sequential-convexifiability criterion fails on this instance precisely when its hypotheses hold but \(R_k\ne H\). The failure is witnessed either by a retained gap point \(z\in R_k\setminus H\) or by loss of validity, meaning \(U\nsubseteq R_j\) for some step \(j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proposed sequential criterion fails when all its hypotheses hold but the resulting relaxation differs from the union hull or excludes a feasible disjunctive point.
assumptions_latex: Each declared relaxation step has a specified operator \(T_j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_k\ne H\), witnessed by \(z\in R_k\setminus H\), or \(U\nsubseteq R_j\) for some \(j\).

notation.meaning: convex hull of the complete union

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No authoritative source or exact sequential-convexifiability criterion is identified. Moreover, the stated operator assumption preserves U at every step, making the proposed loss-of-validity witness impossible under the record's own hypotheses.

children.title: Partial-Convexification Hierarchies
children.top_down_role: Nested relaxations formed by convexifying selected logical subsets.

knowledge_statements.title: Partial-Convexification Hierarchies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Partition-based hierarchy for exact convexification of selected groups of alternatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S_1,\ldots,S_m\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and let \(\Pi\) be a partition of \(I=\{1,\ldots,m\}\). Define the partial convexification \[R(\Pi)=\bigcup_{B\in\Pi}\operatorname{conv}\!\left(\bigcup_{i\in B}S_i\right).\] If \(\Pi_1\) refines \(\Pi_2\), then \(R(\Pi_1)\subseteq R(\Pi_2)\). Thus a chain from the singleton partition to \(\{I\}\) yields nested sets beginning with \(\bigcup_iS_i\) and ending with \(\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_iS_i)\). Intermediate members convexify only alternatives lying in a common block.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coarsening a partition convexifies larger groups of alternatives, producing nested sets from the original union to its full convex hull.
assumptions_latex: \(m\in\mathbb N\) and every \(S_i\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Pi_1\preceq\Pi_2\Longrightarrow R(\Pi_1)\subseteq R(\Pi_2)\), with \(R(\{I\})=\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_iS_i)\).
