children.title: Order-Dependent Convexification Failures
children.top_down_role: Order dependence and failure to recover full convexification.

children.title: Convexification Order
children.top_down_role: Structural influence of operation ordering on sequential convexification.

knowledge_statements.title: Convexification Order
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order is attached to labeled partial operators, including their projection or information-loss conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a relaxation \(R_0\) and partial-convexification operators \(T_1,\ldots,T_k\), a convexification order is a permutation \(\sigma\) of \(\{1,\ldots,k\}\). Its terminal relaxation is \[R^\sigma=T_{\sigma(k)}\circ\cdots\circ T_{\sigma(1)}(R_0).\] Two orders \(\sigma\) and \(\tau\) are equivalent on \(R_0\) when \(R^\sigma=R^\tau\). The operators are order-independent on a class \(\mathcal R\) when this equality holds for every \(R_0\in\mathcal R\) and every pair of permutations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convexification order is a permutation of partial steps; order independence means every permutation gives the same terminal relaxation.
assumptions_latex: Each composition \(T_{\sigma(k)}\circ\cdots\circ T_{\sigma(1)}\) is well-defined on \(R_0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R^\sigma=T_{\sigma(k)}\circ\cdots\circ T_{\sigma(1)}(R_0)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the leaf and is internally coherent, but the labeled partial-operator model and associated order-independence terminology have no cited source.

children.title: Order-Dependent Hull Strength
children.top_down_role: Variation in relaxation strength across convexification orders.

knowledge_statements.title: Order-Dependent Hull Strength
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strength compares terminal relaxations obtained from different orders in the same ambient formulation space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization formulation with terminal relaxations \(R^\sigma,R^\tau\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), order \(\sigma\) is at least as strong as \(\tau\) when \(R^\sigma\subseteq R^\tau\). It is strictly stronger when the inclusion is strict. Consequently, for every objective \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \[\inf_{x\in R^\sigma}c^\top x\geq\inf_{x\in R^\tau}c^\top x.\] If both sets are nonempty closed convex sets and the inclusion is strict, a separating objective gives a strict bound for at least one finite optimization instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One order is stronger when its final relaxation is contained in another's, yielding no weaker minimization bounds for any linear objective.
assumptions_latex: \(R^\sigma\) and \(R^\tau\) use the same original-variable space.
The displayed infima are interpreted in the extended real numbers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R^\sigma\subseteq R^\tau\Longrightarrow \inf_{R^\sigma}c^\top x\geq\inf_{R^\tau}c^\top x\) for every \(c\).

notation.meaning: terminal relaxation produced by order sigma

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Set inclusion correctly implies the displayed extended-real bound inequality. However, strict inclusion of nonempty closed convex sets does not by itself guarantee a separating objective for which both optimization values are finite and strictly different; additional boundedness or finiteness hypotheses are needed. The order-strength framework also lacks a source.

children.title: Nonrecoverable Hull Gaps
children.top_down_role: Residual gaps between sequential results and the target convex hull.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonrecoverable Hull Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A gap is nonrecoverable relative to the remaining admissible operators, not to arbitrary later reformulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=\operatorname{conv}(U)\subseteq R_j\), and let \(\mathcal T_j\) be the admissible remaining partial-convexification operators. The gap at stage \(j\) is nonrecoverable when \[\bigcap_{T\in\langle\mathcal T_j\rangle}T(R_j)\supsetneq H,\] where \(\langle\mathcal T_j\rangle\) contains all finite admissible compositions, including the identity. Equivalently, some \(z\notin H\) belongs to every relaxation reachable from \(R_j\). Such a point certifies that no permitted continuation of the chosen sequence can recover the exact union hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hull gap is nonrecoverable when some point outside the true hull survives every relaxation reachable using the remaining allowed steps.
assumptions_latex: The family of admissible continuations is fixed at stage \(j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists z\in\bigcap_{T\in\langle\mathcal T_j\rangle}T(R_j)\setminus H\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed common-survivor condition is coherent under its assumptions, but “nonrecoverable” and the admissible-composition family are custom to an unsupported operator framework. A source is needed to determine the intended exact definition.

children.title: Irreversible Partial Steps
children.top_down_role: Partial convexification choices that prevent later recovery of the target hull.

knowledge_statements.title: Irreversible Partial Steps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Irreversibility concerns information lost by a partial step under a prescribed family of later operators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) be a partial step applied to state \(R\), and let \(\mathcal S\) be the family of admissible continuations. The step is irreversible relative to \(\mathcal S\) if there exist distinct states \(R_1,R_2\) with \(T(R_1)=T(R_2)\) but the required exact terminal sets differ, and every continuation \(S\in\mathcal S\) depends only on \(T(R_i)\). Then \(S(T(R_1))=S(T(R_2))\) for all \(S\in\mathcal S\), so no such continuation can be exact for both instances. Projection that deletes alternative labels is a typical information-losing step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A partial step is irreversible when it maps distinguishable instances to one state, preventing all later state-based operations from recovering both correct hulls.
assumptions_latex: Later operations receive only the state produced by \(T\).
The two original instances require different exact terminal sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T(R_1)=T(R_2)\Longrightarrow S(T(R_1))=S(T(R_2))\) for every admissible continuation \(S\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The information-loss observation is valid abstractly and failure_boundary fits the leaf, but the instance state, exact-terminal-set map, and admissible continuation model are not formally sourced or fully specified.

children.title: Bounded-Union Representability
children.top_down_role: Mixed-integer representations of finite unions of bounded polyhedral alternatives.

knowledge_statements.title: Bounded-Union Representability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact binary extended formulation for a finite union of nonempty bounded rational polyhedra.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_i=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:A_i x\leq b_i\}\) be nonempty bounded rational polyhedra for \(i=1,\ldots,m\). Then \(\bigcup_iP_i\) is the projection onto \(x\) of \[x=\sum_{i=1}^m x^i,\qquad A_i x^i\leq b_i y_i\ \ (i=1,\ldots,m),\qquad \sum_{i=1}^m y_i=1,\qquad y_i\in\{0,1\}.\] Boundedness gives \(\operatorname{rec}(P_i)=\{0\}\), so \(y_i=0\) forces \(x^i=0\); the unique selected alternative satisfies \(x=x^i\in P_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every finite union of bounded rational polyhedra has an exact binary disjunctive formulation using one scaled copy of each alternative.
assumptions_latex: Each \(P_i\) is nonempty, bounded, and rational.
The union contains finitely many alternatives.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)=\bigcup_{i=1}^mP_i\) for the displayed mixed-integer set \(Q\).

notation.meaning: scaled variable copy for alternative i

children.title: Common-Recession-Cone Regime
children.top_down_role: Representability of unbounded unions sharing compatible recession structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Common-Recession-Cone Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Homogenized disjunctive representation for polyhedra sharing one recession cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_i=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:A_i x\leq b_i\}\) be nonempty rational polyhedra with common recession cone \(C\). Define \(Q\) by \[x=\sum_{i=1}^m x^i,\qquad A_i x^i\leq b_i y_i,\qquad \sum_{i=1}^m y_i=1,\qquad y_i\in\{0,1\}.\] When \(y_k=1\), inactive copies lie in \(C\), while \(x^k\in P_k\); hence \(x\in P_k+C=P_k\). Conversely every point of \(P_k\) is obtained by selecting \(k\). Therefore \(\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)=\bigcup_iP_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Polyhedral alternatives with a common recession cone admit the standard exact homogenized binary formulation despite being unbounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)=\bigcup_{i=1}^mP_i\).

children.title: Incompatible Recession Cones
children.top_down_role: Alternative sets whose unbounded directions lack compatible recession structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Incompatible Recession Cones
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Different recession cones can invalidate the unmodified homogenized binary formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_1=\{(s,0):s\geq0\}\) and \(P_2=\{(0,t):t\geq0\}\). Their recession cones are distinct coordinate rays. In the homogenized formulation \(x=x^1+x^2\), \(x^i\in y_iP_i\) in the homogenized sense, \(y_1+y_2=1\), and \(y\in\{0,1\}^2\), selecting \(y_1=1\) still permits \(x^2\in\operatorname{rec}(P_2)\). Thus every \((s,t)\in\mathbb R_+^2\) is feasible, although \(P_1\cup P_2\) contains only the two axes. The formulation is therefore not exact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For two coordinate rays, inactive recession directions make the standard homogenized binary formulation produce the entire nonnegative quadrant.
assumptions_latex: Scaled sets at zero are interpreted through their homogenized recession cones.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)=\mathbb R_+^2\supsetneq P_1\cup P_2\).

children.title: Nonclosed Union Hulls
children.top_down_role: Convex hulls of unions that fail to be closed.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonclosed Union Hulls
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A finite union of closed polyhedra can have a nonclosed convex hull when recession structures differ.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_1=\{(0,0)\}\) and \(P_2=\{(s,1):s\geq0\}\). Both are closed polyhedra. Their convex hull is \[H=\{(0,0)\}\cup\{(x,y):0<y\leq1,\ x\geq0\}.\] For every \(a>0\), the sequence \((a,1/k)\in H\) converges to \((a,0)\notin H\). Hence \(H\) is not closed, and \[\operatorname{cl}(H)=\{(x,y):x\geq0,\ 0\leq y\leq1\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The hull of a point and a horizontally unbounded ray at height one omits limit points along the positive horizontal axis.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{conv}(P_1\cup P_2)\ne\operatorname{cl}(\operatorname{conv}(P_1\cup P_2))\).

notation.meaning: convex hull of the two polyhedra

children.title: Representability Failure
children.top_down_role: Union structures lacking the targeted mixed-integer representation.

knowledge_statements.title: Representability Failure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary for exact continuous polyhedral extended formulations of the unclosed union hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\subseteq\mathbb R^n\). If \(\operatorname{conv}(U)\) is not closed, then it cannot equal the projection of any finite-dimensional polyhedron \(Q=\{(x,z):Ax+Bz\leq b\}\). Indeed, every linear projection of a polyhedron is a polyhedron and is therefore closed. Consequently, a nonclosed union hull admits no exact finite continuous linear extended formulation; a polyhedral homogenized formulation can represent at most its closure unless additional nonpolyhedral structure or a different target set is used.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonclosed union hull cannot be represented exactly as the projection of a finite continuous linear extended formulation.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\) is a finite-dimensional polyhedron described by finitely many linear inequalities.
The target is \(\operatorname{conv}(U)\), not its closure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{conv}(U)\text{ nonclosed}\Longrightarrow \nexists Q\text{ polyhedral with }\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)=\operatorname{conv}(U)\).

children.title: Closure-Restoration Regimes
children.top_down_role: Structural conditions under which closure can be recovered.

knowledge_statements.title: Closure-Restoration Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Common recession structure or explicit topological closure restores a closed polyhedral hull target.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonempty polyhedra \(P_i=\{x:A_i x\leq b_i\}\), the homogenized continuous formulation \[x=\sum_i x^i,\qquad A_i x^i\leq b_i\lambda_i,\qquad \sum_i\lambda_i=1,\qquad \lambda_i\geq0\] represents \(\operatorname{cl}(\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_iP_i))\). If the \(P_i\) share a common recession cone—bounded alternatives being the special case with cone \(\{0\}\)—the convex hull is already closed, so the closure operator is unnecessary and the formulation represents the hull itself.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Homogenization represents the closed convex hull; a common recession cone, including boundedness, makes this closure coincide with the ordinary union hull.
assumptions_latex: The family \(P_1,\ldots,P_m\) is finite and each member is a nonempty polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)=\operatorname{cl}(\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_iP_i))\), and under a common recession cone this equals \(\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_iP_i)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Full-Disaggregation Formulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex-hull lifting for a finite union of nonempty compact polyhedra.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P_i=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:A_i x\le b_i\}\), for \(i=1,\ldots,k\), be nonempty compact polyhedra. A full-disaggregation formulation of \(x\in\bigcup_{i=1}^kP_i\) is
\[x=\sum_{i=1}^k x^i,\qquad A_i x^i\le b_i\lambda_i\ \ (i=1,\ldots,k),\qquad \sum_{i=1}^k\lambda_i=1,\qquad \lambda\in\{0,1\}^k.\]
Every alternative has a complete local copy \(x^i\). The integer-feasible projection onto \(x\) equals \(\bigcup_iP_i\); replacing \(\lambda\in\{0,1\}^k\) by \(\lambda\ge0\) yields projection \(\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_iP_i)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each alternative receives a complete variable copy. Binary selection represents the union exactly, while continuous selection projects to its convex hull.
assumptions_latex: \(k<\infty\) and every \(P_i\) is nonempty and compact.
Each alternative uses the same ambient space \(\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_x(F_{\mathrm{int}})=\bigcup_iP_i\) and \(\operatorname{proj}_x(F_{\mathrm{LP}})=\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_iP_i)\).

children.title: Partial-Disaggregation Formulations

knowledge_statements.title: Partial-Disaggregation Formulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selective copying for alternatives that share a separable common variable block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose each alternative has the product form \(P_i=U_i\times Q\), where \(U_i=\{u\in\mathbb R^p:B_i u\le d_i\}\) is nonempty and compact and \(Q\subseteq\mathbb R^q\) is common. Then membership of \((u,z)\) in \(\bigcup_iP_i\) is represented by
\[u=\sum_{i=1}^k u^i,\qquad B_i u^i\le d_i\lambda_i,\qquad z\in Q,\qquad \sum_{i=1}^k\lambda_i=1,
\qquad \lambda\in\{0,1\}^k.\]
Only the alternative-dependent block \(u\) is copied. With \(\lambda\ge0\), the projection is \(\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_iU_i)\times Q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When alternatives differ only in one separable variable block, copying that block alone gives an exact union model and preserves the corresponding convex-hull relaxation.
assumptions_latex: \(P_i=U_i\times Q\) with the same nonempty convex set \(Q\) for every alternative.
Each \(U_i\) is a nonempty compact polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The integer projection is \(\bigcup_i(U_i\times Q)\), and its relaxation projects to \(\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_iU_i)\times Q\).

children.title: Parsimonious Multiple-Choice Formulations
children.top_down_role: Alternative-selection formulations designed to limit auxiliary structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Parsimonious Multiple-Choice Formulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-hot big-M representation using no alternative-local continuous copies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be bounded and let \(P_i=\{x\in X:a_{ij}^{\mathsf T}x\le b_{ij},\ j\in J_i\}\) for \(i=1,\ldots,k\). Choose finite constants satisfying \(M_{ij}\ge\max_{x\in X}(a_{ij}^{\mathsf T}x-b_{ij})\). The parsimonious multiple-choice formulation is
\[x\in X,\qquad a_{ij}^{\mathsf T}x\le b_{ij}+M_{ij}(1-y_i),\qquad \sum_{i=1}^k y_i=1,\qquad y\in\{0,1\}^k.\]
Denote this formulation by \(F_{\mathrm{int}}\) and its relaxation obtained by replacing \(y\in\{0,1\}^k\) with \(y\in[0,1]^k\) by \(F_{\mathrm{LP}}\). It uses one shared vector \(x\) and one selector per alternative. Its integer projection is exactly \(\bigcup_{i=1}^kP_i\), while its continuous relaxation contains \(\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_{i=1}^kP_i)\) and may contain it strictly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Valid big-M inequalities and one-hot selectors represent the union without copied continuous variables. The continuous relaxation contains the convex hull and can be strictly weaker, although equality is possible.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is bounded and contains every alternative.
Every \(M_{ij}\) is a valid upper bound on the corresponding constraint violation over \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_x(F_{\mathrm{int}})=\bigcup_{i=1}^kP_i\) and \(\operatorname{proj}_x(F_{\mathrm{LP}})\supseteq\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_{i=1}^kP_i)\), with strict containment possible.

children.title: Nonlinear Hull Formulations
children.top_down_role: Perspective-based extended formulations for convex nonlinear alternatives.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonlinear Hull Formulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed-perspective hull formulation for compact convex nonlinear alternatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each \(i\), let \(C_i=\{x\in[\ell_i,u_i]:g_{ij}(x)\le0,\ j\in J_i\}\) be nonempty and compact, with every \(g_{ij}\) closed and convex. Define its closed perspective by \(\widetilde g_{ij}(v,\lambda)=\operatorname{cl}(\lambda g_{ij}(v/\lambda))\). Then
\[x=\sum_i v^i,\quad \lambda_i\ell_i\le v^i\le\lambda_i u_i,\quad \widetilde g_{ij}(v^i,\lambda_i)\le0,\quad \sum_i\lambda_i=1.\]
With \(\lambda\in\{0,1\}^k\), this represents \(x\in\bigcup_iC_i\); with \(\lambda\ge0\), its projection is \(\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_iC_i)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Closed perspectives scale each convex nonlinear alternative. Binary weights model the union exactly, and continuous weights produce its convex hull.
assumptions_latex: Each \(C_i\) is nonempty, compact, and convex.
Each defining function \(g_{ij}\) is proper, closed, and convex.
Finite componentwise bounds \(\ell_i,u_i\) are valid for \(C_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The binary formulation projects to \(\bigcup_iC_i\), while its continuous relaxation projects to \(\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_iC_i)\).

children.title: Unary Coordinate Encodings

knowledge_statements.title: Unary Coordinate Encodings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate-vector codes for alternatives in a finite disjunction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(k\) alternatives, the unary coordinate code assigns alternative \(i\) the vector \(h^i=e^i\in\{0,1\}^k\), where \(e^i_i=1\) and \(e^i_j=0\) for \(j\ne i\). Thus the code set is
\[H_{\mathrm{unary}}=\{e^1,\ldots,e^k\}.\]
For sets \(P_i\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), the associated embedded union is \(E=\bigcup_{i=1}^k(P_i\times\{e^i\})\). Every code has exactly one active coordinate, and distinct codes have Hamming distance two.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unary encoding labels each alternative by its own unit coordinate. Every label has one active bit, and any two labels differ in two positions.
assumptions_latex: The disjunction has a finite indexed alternative set \(\{1,\ldots,k\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H_{\mathrm{unary}}=\{h\in\{0,1\}^k:\sum_{j=1}^k h_j=1\}\) and \(d_H(e^i,e^j)=2\) for \(i\ne j\).

children.title: One-Hot Selection Encodings

knowledge_statements.title: One-Hot Selection Encodings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary selector representation of exactly one active alternative.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A one-hot selection encoding for \(k\) alternatives is a vector \(y\in\{0,1\}^k\) satisfying
\[\sum_{i=1}^k y_i=1.\]
Alternative \(i\) is selected precisely when \(y_i=1\). Consequently the feasible selector set equals \(\{e^1,
\ldots,e^k\}\). Its continuous relaxation is the simplex \(\Delta_k=\{y\in\mathbb R_+^k:\sum_i y_i=1\}\), whose extreme points are exactly the one-hot vectors; hence the selector subsystem itself is integral.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A one-hot selector is binary and sums to one. Its relaxation is the standard simplex, whose vertices are exactly the valid selection vectors.
assumptions_latex: There are exactly \(k\) mutually exclusive alternatives and one must be selected.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selector set is \(\{e^1,\ldots,e^k\}\), and \(\operatorname{ext}(\Delta_k)=\{e^1,\ldots,e^k\}\).

notation.meaning: indicator that alternative i is selected

children.title: Unary–One-Hot Correspondence

knowledge_statements.title: Unary–One-Hot Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identity correspondence between unary embedding labels and one-hot selectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let unary code \(h^i=e^i\) label alternative \(i\), and let \(y\in\{0,1\}^k\) satisfy \(\sum_i y_i=1\). The correspondence is the identity map
\[y=e^i\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad h=h^i\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad y_i=1.\]
Accordingly,
\[\bigcup_{i=1}^k(P_i\times\{h^i\})=\{(x,y):y\in\{0,1\}^k,\ \sum_i y_i=1,\ x\in P_i\text{ for the unique }i\text{ with }y_i=1\}.\]
Thus unary coordinates used as embedding labels and one-hot variables used as selectors encode the same alternatives without a change of code space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unary labels and one-hot selectors are the same unit vectors; identifying their coordinates gives a bijection preserving the selected alternative.
assumptions_latex: Both encodings use the same ordering of the \(k\) alternatives.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The map \(h\mapsto y=h\) is a bijection between unary codes and feasible one-hot selectors and preserves alternative membership.

children.title: Binary Embedding Codes

knowledge_statements.title: Binary Embedding Codes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Injective binary labels for a finite family of alternatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A binary embedding code for \(k\) alternatives is an injective assignment \(i\mapsto h^i\) with \(h^i\in\{0,1\}^r\). Necessarily \(2^r\ge k\), so \(r\ge\lceil\log_2 k\rceil\), and this lower bound is attainable. For sets \(P_i\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), the code defines the embedded union
\[E_H=\bigcup_{i=1}^k(P_i\times\{h^i\})\]
and its embedding polytope \(Q_H=\operatorname{conv}(E_H)\). Requiring the code variable to equal a member of \(H=\{h^1,\ldots,h^k\}\) recovers the associated alternative from the embedded representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An injective binary code labels each alternative. At least the ceiling of log base two of the alternative count is required, and this many bits suffice.
assumptions_latex: The number of alternatives \(k\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An injective code exists in \(\{0,1\}^r\) if and only if \(2^r\ge k\).

notation.meaning: finite set of assigned binary codewords

children.title: Gray-Code Embeddings
children.top_down_role: Compact embeddings whose neighboring alternatives receive adjacent codewords.

knowledge_statements.title: Gray-Code Embeddings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reflected Gray labels for an ordered finite disjunction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(r=\lceil\log_2 k\rceil\) and index alternatives by \(i=0,\ldots,k-1\). The reflected binary Gray code assigns
\[h^i=\operatorname{bin}_r\!\left(i\mathbin{\mathrm{xor}}\left\lfloor i/2\right\rfloor\right)\in\{0,1\}^r,\]
where \(\operatorname{bin}_r\) is the length-\(r\) binary expansion. The Gray-code embedding is \(E_G=\bigcup_{i=0}^{k-1}(P_i\times\{h^i\})\). The assignment is injective and satisfies \(d_H(h^i,h^{i+1})=1\) for every \(i=0,\ldots,k-2\), while using the minimum possible binary code dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reflected Gray code injectively labels ordered alternatives with the minimum number of bits, and consecutive alternatives differ in exactly one bit.
assumptions_latex:
Alternatives have a fixed linear order \(0,
\ldots,k-1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The Gray assignment is injective, has dimension \(\lceil\log_2k\rceil\), and obeys \(d_H(h^i,h^{i+1})=1\).

children.title: Code Adjacency Effects
children.top_down_role: Formulation consequences associated with codeword proximity across alternatives.

knowledge_statements.title: Code Adjacency Effects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of codeword distance on one-bit transitions between alternatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an injective binary code \(H=\{h^1,\ldots,h^k\}\subseteq\{0,1\}^r\), form the code graph with an edge \(\{i,j\}\) exactly when \(d_H(h^i,h^j)=1\). A change from alternative \(i\) to alternative \(j\) can be made by changing one code coordinate while remaining at a valid codeword exactly when \(\{i,j\}\) is an edge. Hence a Gray assignment makes every consecutive ordered pair adjacent. If \(d_H(h^i,h^j)>1\), no direct one-coordinate change connects those alternatives; any coordinatewise path requires intermediate binary vectors or simultaneous changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hamming-distance-one codewords permit direct one-bit transitions. Gray coding guarantees this adjacency for consecutive alternatives; more distant codes require intermediate or simultaneous bit changes.
assumptions_latex: A direct transition changes exactly one binary coordinate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Alternatives \(i\) and \(j\) admit a direct one-coordinate code transition if and only if \(d_H(h^i,h^j)=1\).

children.title: Ideal Embedding Families

knowledge_statements.title: Ideal Embedding Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ideality criterion for extended formulations of code-embedded disjunctions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(E_H=\bigcup_i(P_i\times\{h^i\})\), with integral codewords \(h^i\in\mathbb Z^r\), and let \(R\) be a polyhedral extended formulation projecting onto \(E_H\) after imposing code integrality. The formulation is ideal when every extreme point of its linear relaxation has an integral projected code vector:
\[v\in\operatorname{ext}(R)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \operatorname{proj}_h(v)\in\mathbb Z^r.\]
An ideal embedding family is a collection of such formulations indexed by code sets or disjunctions. Members may trade code dimension, auxiliary variables, and inequality count while retaining this integrality property.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An embedding formulation is ideal when every relaxation vertex has an integral code. An ideal family preserves this property while varying code size or formulation size.
assumptions_latex: Imposing integrality on the code variables yields the intended embedded disjunction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Ideality holds exactly when \(\operatorname{proj}_h(v)\in\mathbb Z^r\) for every \(v\in\operatorname{ext}(R)\).

children.title: Embedding-Code Symmetry
children.top_down_role: Equivalent code assignments and associated search redundancy.

knowledge_statements.title: Embedding-Code Symmetry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine equivalence induced by permuting or complementing binary code coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H=\{h^1,\ldots,h^k\}\subseteq\{0,1\}^r\). Let \(T\) permute code coordinates and independently complement any coordinates, and let \(\sigma\) permute alternative labels. Define \(\widehat h^{\sigma(i)}=T(h^i)\) and \(\widehat P_{
\sigma(i)}=P_i\). Then
\[\operatorname{conv}\!\left(\bigcup_i P_i\times\{h^i\}\right)\]
is mapped affinely and bijectively onto
\[\operatorname{conv}\!\left(\bigcup_j\widehat P_j\times\{\widehat h^j\}\right)\]
by \((x,h)\mapsto(x,T(h))\). Thus these code transformations preserve dimension, face structure, and ideality, so searching all symmetry-equivalent assignments is redundant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coordinate permutations, bit complements, and consistent alternative relabelings produce affinely equivalent embedding polytopes and therefore redundant code assignments.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is generated by binary-coordinate permutations and complements.
Alternative sets are relabeled consistently by the permutation \(\sigma\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The two embedding polytopes are affinely isomorphic; consequently dimension, face lattice, and formulation ideality are preserved.

children.title: Cayley Polytope Formulations
children.top_down_role: Cayley constructions used to represent unions through lifted polyhedral structure.

assumptions_latex: \(P_i\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is a nonempty polytope for each \(i\in[k]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q_H=\operatorname{conv}\bigl(\bigcup_{i=1}^k(P_i\times\{h^i\})\bigr)\) is the Cayley polytope, and \(\{x:(x,h^i)\in Q_H\}=P_i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite unions of bounded polyhedra with code points in convex position.

source_refs.locator: 2.1 The Convex Hull Via Lifting and Projection p. 17

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(i\in[k]\), assign alternative \(P_i\) the code \(h^i\). Its Cayley embedding is
\[
Q_H:=\operatorname{conv}\left(\bigcup_{i=1}^k(P_i\times\{h^i\})\right).
\]
Because every \(h^i\) is a vertex of \(\operatorname{conv}(H)\), the code fiber satisfies \(\{x:(x,h^i)\in Q_H\}=P_i\). Hence
\[
\operatorname{proj}_x\bigl(Q_H\cap(\mathbb{R}^n\times H)\bigr)=\bigcup_{i=1}^kP_i.
\]
Thus a linear description of \(Q_H\), together with the restriction \(z\in H\), is an exact coded formulation of the disjunction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Cayley polytope is the convex hull of alternatives tagged by vertex codes; restricting the code to its finite code set recovers exactly the original union.

children.title: Embedding–Cayley Correspondence

knowledge_statements.title: Embedding–Cayley Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correspondence between finite code embeddings and Cayley convexification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
E:=\bigcup_{i=1}^k(P_i\times\{h^i\}).
\]
The embedding convexification and the Cayley construction coincide:
\[
\operatorname{conv}(E)=\operatorname{Cay}(P,H):=\left\{\left(\sum_{i=1}^k\lambda_i x^i,\sum_{i=1}^k\lambda_i h^i\right):\lambda\in\Delta_k,\ x^i\in P_i\text{ for all }i\in[k]\right\}.
\]
Moreover, \(E=\operatorname{Cay}(P,H)\cap(\mathbb{R}^n\times H)\). Consequently, an inequality description of either convex hull gives the same continuous relaxation and the same code fibers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convexifying a union of code-tagged alternatives is exactly the Cayley construction; intersecting it with the discrete code set restores the embedded union.
assumptions_latex: \(P_i\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is a nonempty polytope for every \(i\in[k]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{conv}(E)=\operatorname{Cay}(P,H)\) and \(E=\operatorname{Cay}(P,H)\cap(\mathbb{R}^n\times H)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A hybrid formulation uses \(y\in\{0,1\}^k\), copies \(v_i\), and
\[
\sum_i y_i=1,\qquad x=\sum_i v_i,\qquad A_i^Hv_i\le b_i^Hy_i,\qquad A_i^Mx\le b_i^M+M_i(1-y_i).
\]
Appropriate scaled-domain constraints on \(v_i\) impose \(v_i=0\) when \(y_i=0\). For binary \(y\), the projection is \(\bigcup_iP_i\). With \(y\in\Delta_k\), the relaxation combines hull strength for the selected rows with big-M strength for the remaining rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The hybrid formulation applies disaggregated hull lifting to selected constraints and valid big-M activation to the rest, preserving the original integer disjunction.
knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Big-M–Hull Formulations

children.title: Partition Linking Relations
children.top_down_role: Relations coordinating variables or selections across lifted partitions.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal{G}\) is a partition of the alternative index set \([k]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The aggregate relations \(z_G=\sum_{i\in G}y_i\) and compatible variable decompositions link group and alternative levels without changing integer projections.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency equations connecting alternative selectors, group selectors, and partially disaggregated variable copies.

source_refs.locator: 2.1 The Convex Hull Via Lifting and Projection p. 17

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(G\in\mathcal{G}\), introduce a group selector and impose
\[
z_G=\sum_{i\in G}y_i,\qquad \sum_{G\in\mathcal{G}}z_G=1.
\]
If \(x^G\) and \(v_i\) are group- and alternative-level copies, respectively, impose
\[
x=\sum_{G\in\mathcal{G}}x^G,\qquad x^G=\sum_{i\in G}v_i.
\]
These are partition linking relations. They are valid for every embedded representation using the same selectors and enforce consistency between aggregation levels; eliminating \(z\) and \(x^G\) restores the alternative-level linking equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partition linking relations equate each group activation and group variable copy to the sums of their alternative-level counterparts.

children.title: Cross-Disjunct Valid Inequalities
children.top_down_role: Strengthening relations that use information shared across multiple alternatives.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selector-lifted inequality \(\alpha^Tx\le\sum_i\beta_i y_i\) is valid for every exact one-hot formulation of the disjunction.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selector-dependent lifting of inequalities sharing a common left-hand side across alternatives.

source_refs.locator: 1.4 Valid Inequalities for Disjunctive Sets p. 9

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(y\in\{0,1\}^k\) satisfy \(\sum_i y_i=1\), with \(y_i=1\) selecting \(P_i\). If \(\alpha^Tx\le\beta_i\) holds for every \(x\in P_i\), then
\[
\alpha^Tx\le\sum_{i=1}^k\beta_i y_i
\]
is valid for the embedded disjunction. Its projection implies the union-valid inequality \(\alpha^Tx\le\max_i\beta_i\), while retaining \(y\) preserves the stronger alternative-dependent right-hand side.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternative-specific bounds with a common left side combine into a selector-weighted inequality that couples all disjuncts and dominates the projected maximum bound.

assumptions_latex: The coordinate partition is \(\{\{1\},\{2\}\}\), and each block uses independent alternative weights.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Independent block convexification yields \([0,1]^2\), strictly larger than \(\operatorname{conv}(P_1\cup P_2)=\{(t,t):0\le t\le1\}\).

notation.meaning: Independent weight for coordinate block j.
Convex hull of the original union.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp loss of cross-block dependence when partition blocks do not share linking weights.

source_refs.locator: 5.1 Comparing the Strength of Different Formulations p. 70

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The true disjunctive hull is
\[
C=\operatorname{conv}(P_1\cup P_2)=\{(t,t):0\le t\le1\}.
\]
If each singleton coordinate block is convexified with an independent weight, the resulting relaxation is
\[
\{(t_1,t_2):0\le t_1\le1,\ 0\le t_2\le1\}=[0,1]^2.
\]
Thus \((0,1)\) is admitted although it is not in \(C\). Shared alternative weights or equivalent cross-block linking relations are therefore necessary in general; separate block validity alone cannot recover cross-disjunct dependence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent block convexifications can destroy cross-coordinate dependence: two diagonal singleton alternatives relax to the whole unit square unless their mixture weights are linked.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Multiplier Certificate for Polyhedral Containment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes containment of a nonempty polyhedral relaxation in another polyhedron by a nonnegative multiplier certificate for every defining row of the latter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_1:=\{(x,y):A_1x+G_1y\le b_1\}\ne\varnothing\) and \(P_2:=\{(x,y):A_2x+G_2y\le b_2\}\). children.title: Reformulation Validity
children.top_down_role: Preservation of admissible modeled outcomes under reformulation.

assumptions_latex: \(S\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is the feasible set of the original model.
\(Q\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n+p+q}\) uses original variables \(x\), continuous auxiliaries \(u\), and integer auxiliaries \(z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q\) is a valid reformulation precisely when \(\operatorname{proj}_x(Q\cap(\mathbb{R}^{n+p}\times\mathbb{Z}^q))=S\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible-set validity of an extended mixed-integer reformulation under projection.

source_refs.locator: 1.6 Alternative Formulations p. 12

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The lifted set \(Q\) is a valid reformulation of \(S\) when
\[
\operatorname{proj}_x\left(Q\cap(\mathbb{R}^{n+p}\times\mathbb{Z}^q)\right)=S.
\]
Equivalently, every integer-feasible lifted point projects to an original feasible point, and every \(x\in S\) has at least one feasible lift \((x,u,z)\in Q\) with \(z\in\mathbb{Z}^q\). For any objective depending only on \(x\), this equality preserves feasibility and the optimal value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lifted mixed-integer model is a valid reformulation exactly when projecting all integer-feasible lifted points gives the original feasible set.
knowledge_statements.title: Reformulation Validity

children.title: Logical Equivalence
children.top_down_role: Agreement between the intended logical alternatives and the encoded alternatives.

assumptions_latex: \(S_i\) denotes the feasible set of logical alternative \(i\in[k]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Logical equivalence holds exactly when \(\operatorname{proj}_x\{(x,w):(x,w,e^i)\in Q\}=S_i\) for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Alternative-by-alternative equivalence between selector truth assignments and disjunct feasibility.

source_refs.locator: Generalized disjunctive programming: A framework for formulation and alternative algorithms for MINLP optimization p. 93

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A one-hot reformulation is logically equivalent to the disjunction when, for every \(i\in[k]\),
\[
\operatorname{proj}_x\{(x,w):(x,w,e^i)\in Q\}=S_i.
\]
Hence \(y_i=1\) is feasible if and only if the original variables satisfy alternative \(i\). Taking the union over unit vectors then gives
\[
\operatorname{proj}_x\{(x,w,y)\in Q:y\in\{e^1,\ldots,e^k\}\}=\bigcup_{i=1}^kS_i.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Logical equivalence requires each one-hot selector assignment to have exactly the same projected feasible points as its corresponding logical alternative.

children.title: Projection Fidelity
children.top_down_role: Consistency of represented outcomes after auxiliary variables are removed.

assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is the intended continuous relaxation of the original feasible set.
\(R\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n+p}\) is the continuous relaxation of an extended formulation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The extended relaxation has projection fidelity precisely when \(\operatorname{proj}_x(R)=C\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact equality between a lifted continuous relaxation and its intended original-space projection.

source_refs.locator: 2.3 Projection with a Minimal System of Inequalities p. 31

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Projection fidelity relative to \(C\) is the equality
\[
\operatorname{proj}_x(R)=\{x:\exists u\text{ with }(x,u)\in R\}=C.
\]
The inclusion \(C\subseteq\operatorname{proj}_x(R)\) prevents loss of intended points, while \(\operatorname{proj}_x(R)\subseteq C\) prevents spurious projected points. When \(C=\operatorname{conv}(S)\), projection fidelity means that the extended continuous relaxation projects exactly to the convex hull of the original feasible set \(S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection fidelity means the continuous lifted model projects to exactly the intended original-space relaxation, neither deleting valid points nor introducing spurious ones.
knowledge_statements.title: Projection Fidelity

children.title: Spurious Alternative Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Failure cases where a reformulation admits unintended logical regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Spurious Alternative Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fiber-level boundary separating exact alternative encoding from unintended selector states or projected points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a selector value \(y\), define the projected fiber
\[
Q_y:=\{x:\exists w\text{ with }(x,w,y)\in Q\}.
\]
A spurious alternative or spurious alternative point occurs whenever either \(Q_y\ne\varnothing\) for an admissible integer selector \(y\notin Y\), or \(Q_{e^i}\not\subseteq S_i\) for some \(i\in[k]\). Thus absence of spurious alternatives requires every admissible integer selector to lie in \(Y\) and \(Q_{e^i}\subseteq S_i\) for all \(i\in[k]\). Exact logical equivalence additionally requires \(Q_{e^i}=S_i\) for every \(i\in[k]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Spurious alternatives arise when an unintended integer selector has a feasible fiber or a legal selector fiber contains points outside its intended disjunct; equality of every legal fiber with its disjunct is the stronger requirement of logical equivalence.
assumptions_latex: \(k\) is a positive integer, \(S_i\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) for \(i\in[k]\), and \(S=\bigcup_{i=1}^kS_i\).
\(Q\) is a lifted formulation in variables \((x,w,y)\), and \(Y=\{e^1,\ldots,e^k\}\) is the intended one-hot selector set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Absence of spurious alternatives requires \(Q_y=\varnothing\) for every admissible integer \(y\notin Y\) and \(Q_{e^i}\subseteq S_i\) for every \(i\in[k]\); exact logical equivalence requires \(Q_{e^i}=S_i\).

notation.meaning: Projected fiber of the lifted formulation at selector value y.

knowledge_statements.title: Ideal Formulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polyhedral mixed-integer formulations whose continuous-relaxation vertices satisfy all designated integrality restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A valid mixed-integer formulation is ideal if every extreme point \((x,z)\) of its continuous relaxation \(R\) satisfies \(z\in\mathbb{Z}^q\). Consequently, whenever a linear objective has a finite optimum over \(R\) that is attained at an extreme point, at least one optimal solution satisfies the formulation's designated integrality restrictions without branching.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An ideal formulation is valid and has integral designated variables at every extreme point of its continuous relaxation; therefore any linear optimum attained at an extreme point has an integral designated-variable optimum.
assumptions_latex: \(Q=\{(x,z)\in\mathbb{R}^{n+q}:Ax+Bz\le d,\ z\in\mathbb{Z}^q\}\) is a valid formulation of \(S\).
\(R=\{(x,z)\in\mathbb{R}^{n+q}:Ax+Bz\le d\}\) is the continuous polyhedral relaxation of \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The formulation is ideal when every extreme point \((x,z)\) of \(R\) satisfies \(z\in\mathbb{Z}^q\).

knowledge_statements.title: Sharp Formulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected-relaxation definition for a lifted mixed-integer formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be the represented set, and let \(Q\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^r\) be the continuous relaxation of an exact lifted mixed-integer formulation, so that \(S=\operatorname{proj}_x(Q\cap(\mathbb{R}^n\times Z))\) for the prescribed integrality set \(Z\). The formulation is sharp with respect to the original variables when
\[\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)=\operatorname{conv}(S).\]
Thus its continuous relaxation gives the convex hull after projection, although \(Q\) itself may have fractional auxiliary extreme points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lifted formulation is sharp when projecting its continuous relaxation onto the original variables yields exactly the convex hull of the represented set.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\) is a polyhedron and the mixed-integer formulation represents \(S\) exactly.
\(\operatorname{conv}(S)\) is interpreted in the original-variable space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)=\operatorname{conv}(S)\).

children.title: Perfect Formulations

knowledge_statements.title: Perfect Formulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Original-space perfect formulation of an integer-feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S\subseteq\mathbb{Z}^p\times\mathbb{R}^q\), and let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^{p+q}:Ax\le b\}\) be an exact original-space formulation, meaning \(S=P\cap(\mathbb{Z}^p\times\mathbb{R}^q)\). The formulation is perfect when
\[P=\operatorname{conv}(S).\]
Equivalently, every linear objective having a finite optimum over \(P\) has the same optimal value over \(S\); when the optimum is attained, an optimal point can be chosen from \(S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact original-space formulation is perfect when its polyhedron equals the convex hull of its mixed-integer feasible points.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) represents \(S\) exactly in the original variables.
Linear objectives under consideration have finite optima.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P=\operatorname{conv}(S)\).

children.title: Quality-Class Separations
children.top_down_role: Distinctions and overlap among the ideal, sharp, and perfect classes.

knowledge_statements.title: Quality-Class Separations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation between projected sharpness and auxiliary-variable ideality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S=\{0,1\}\) and
\[Q=\operatorname{conv}\{(0,0,0),(1,1,0),(1/2,1/2,1)\}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^3,\]
with coordinates \((x,z,w)\), where only \(z\) is required to be integral. Then \(\operatorname{proj}_x(Q\cap\{z\in\mathbb{Z}\})=S\) and \(\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)=[0,1]=\operatorname{conv}(S)\), so the formulation is sharp. Nevertheless, \((1/2,1/2,1)\) is an extreme point of \(Q\) with fractional integer-designated coordinate \(z=1/2\); hence the formulation is not ideal. Therefore sharpness does not imply ideality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lifted relaxation can project to the exact hull while retaining a fractional extreme point in an integer-designated auxiliary variable; sharpness therefore need not imply ideality.
assumptions_latex: Ideality means that every extreme point of the relaxation has integral values in all integer-designated coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{sharp}\not\Rightarrow\text{ideal}\) for lifted formulations.

children.title: Dominance Between Formulations
children.top_down_role: Comparison of relaxation strength among equivalent representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Dominance Between Formulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relaxation-strength comparison after projection to common variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F_1\) and \(F_2\) be exact formulations of the same set \(S\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), with continuous relaxations \(Q_1\) and \(Q_2\), possibly in different extended spaces. Formulation \(F_1\) dominates \(F_2\) in relaxation strength when
\[\operatorname{proj}_x(Q_1)\subseteq\operatorname{proj}_x(Q_2).\]
Dominance is strict when this inclusion is proper. Consequently, for every \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\),
\[\inf\{c^Tx:x\in\operatorname{proj}_x(Q_1)\}\ge \inf\{c^Tx:x\in\operatorname{proj}_x(Q_2)\},\]
with the inequality interpreted in the extended real numbers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One exact formulation dominates another when its projected continuous relaxation is contained in the other's; it consequently supplies at least as strong every linear minimization bound.
assumptions_latex: Both mixed-integer formulations represent the same original-variable set \(S\).
The relaxations are compared after projection onto the same original-variable space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_1\succeq F_2\iff\operatorname{proj}_x(Q_1)\subseteq\operatorname{proj}_x(Q_2)\).

notation.meaning: continuous relaxation of the ith formulation

children.title: Size–Strength–Inference Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Interactions among relaxation quality, representation size, propagation, and solver workload.

knowledge_statements.title: Size–Strength–Inference Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pareto comparison of formulation size, relaxation strength, and propagation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For an exact formulation \(F\), let \(s(F)\) be its encoded size, \(R(F)\) its projected continuous relaxation, and \(I_F(B)\) the variable-domain deductions obtained by a fixed inference procedure from an input box \(B\). A formulation \(F_1\) Pareto-dominates \(F_2\) under these criteria if
\[s(F_1)\le s(F_2),\qquad R(F_1)\subseteq R(F_2),\qquad I_{F_1}(B)\subseteq I_{F_2}(B)\ \text{for every }B,\]
where smaller inferred boxes are stronger, and at least one comparison is strict. Absent such dominance or an explicit weighting, size, strength, and inference do not define a unique quality ordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Formulation quality is naturally Pareto-valued: a formulation is unambiguously better only when it is no larger, has a tighter relaxation, and yields no weaker fixed-procedure deductions.
assumptions_latex: Encoded size is measured under one fixed encoding convention.
Both formulations use the same original variables and the same inference procedure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((s,R,I)\) induces a partial, generally not total, formulation-quality order.

notation.meaning: box remaining after the fixed inference procedure

children.title: Alternative-Selection Encoding Complexity
children.top_down_role: Unary, logarithmic, and structurally compressed encodings of alternatives.

knowledge_statements.title: Alternative-Selection Encoding Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary-variable information bound for selecting one of finitely many alternatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(k\ge2\) alternatives must receive distinct assignments of \(b\) binary selector variables. Since \(b\) bits have at most \(2^b\) assignments, every injective binary encoding satisfies
\[b\ge\lceil\log_2 k\rceil.\]
A logarithmic encoding attains this bound by assigning distinct bit vectors to the alternatives, whereas a unary one-hot encoding uses \(k\) binaries satisfying \(\sum_{i=1}^k y_i=1\). Structural compression may replace \(k\) by the number \(m\) of distinguishable feasible alternative classes, but then still requires at least \(\lceil\log_2 m\rceil\) unrestricted binary bits.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Selecting among k distinguishable alternatives needs at least ceiling(log2 k) binary bits; logarithmic codes attain this information bound, while one-hot selection uses k binaries.
assumptions_latex: Each distinguishable alternative must have a distinct binary code.
Complexity counts unrestricted binary selector variables, not inequalities or coefficient encoding length.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(b\ge\lceil\log_2 k\rceil\), with equality attainable at the code-assignment level.

children.title: Disjunctive Duality
children.top_down_role: Dual viewpoints for optimization and validity over unions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual of a Disjunctive Linear Program
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the disjunctive primal and dual together with the branchwise feasible and homogeneous systems used in subsequent regularity and duality statements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For data \(c,A^h,b^h\) indexed by \(h\in Q\), let
\[
X_h=\{x:A^hx\ge b^h,\ x\ge0\},\qquad z_0=\min\{cx:x\in\bigcup_{h\in Q}X_h\}.
\]
The dual of this disjunctive program is
\[
w_0=\max_{w,(u^h)}\left\{w:w-u^hb^h\le0,\ u^hA^h\le c,\ u^h\ge0\quad\forall h\in Q\right\}.
\]
Define
\[
\bar X_h=\{x:A^hx\ge0,\ x\ge0\},\quad U_h=\{u^h:u^hA^h\le c,\ u^h\ge0\},\quad \bar U_h=\{u^h:u^hA^h\le0,\ u^h\ge0\},
\]
and
\[
Q^*=\{h\in Q:X_h\ne\varnothing\},\qquad Q^{**}=\{h\in Q:U_h\ne\varnothing\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The primal minimizes cx over the union of the systems A^h x ≥ b^h, x ≥ 0. Its dual maximizes a common scalar w subject, for every h, to w ≤ u^h b^h, u^h A^h ≤ c, and u^h ≥ 0. The sets X_h, bar X_h, U_h, and bar U_h describe the branchwise primal, homogeneous-primal, dual, and homogeneous-dual systems; Q* and Q** index the nonempty X_h and U_h sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (DD):\quad w_0=\max\{w:w\le u^hb^h,\ u^hA^h\le c,\ u^h\ge0\ \forall h\in Q\},\quad Q^*=\{h:X_h\ne\varnothing\},\quad Q^{**}=\{h:U_h\ne\varnothing\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Duality-Gap Regime When Regularity Fails
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Records the stated failure regime for a feasible disjunctive primal and infeasible dual when the regularity condition fails.

If the disjunctive-duality regularity condition does not hold, then

Thus the primal may have a finite attained optimum while the dual is infeasible.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Regularity Condition for Disjunctive Duality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the regularity hypothesis for the disjunctive primal-dual pair; it is distinct from regular-versus-irregular disjunctive-cut classifications.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
Q^*=\{h\in Q:X_h\ne\varnothing\},\qquad Q^{**}=\{h\in Q:U_h\ne\varnothing\}.
\]
The regularity condition is
\[
\bigl(Q^*\ne\varnothing\ \land\ Q\setminus Q^{**}\ne\varnothing\bigr)\implies Q^*\setminus Q^{**}\ne\varnothing.
\]
Equivalently, if \((DP)\) is feasible and \((DD)\) is infeasible, then there exists \(h\in Q\) such that \(X_h\ne\varnothing\) and \(U_h=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the disjunctive primal is feasible and the disjunctive dual is infeasible, at least one alternative must have a nonempty primal feasible set and an empty corresponding dual-multiplier set.

children.title: Multiplier Certificates for Unions
children.top_down_role: Dual certificates supporting restrictions valid across alternatives.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier Certificates for Unions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Farkas multiplier certificate for validity over a finite polyhedral union.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P_i=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:A_i x\le b_i\}\), for \(i=1,\ldots,k\), be nonempty polyhedra, and let \((\alpha,\beta)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}\). Assume that \(\sup\{\alpha^Tx:x\in P_i\}\) is finite for every \(i\). Then \(\alpha^Tx\le\beta\) is valid for \(\bigcup_{i=1}^kP_i\) if and only if, for every \(i\), there exists \(\lambda_i\ge0\) satisfying
\[A_i^T\lambda_i=\alpha,\qquad b_i^T\lambda_i\le\beta.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under finite support in the specified direction, a linear inequality is valid across a finite polyhedral union exactly when every alternative admits nonnegative multipliers deriving that inequality from its defining system.
assumptions_latex: The support value in direction \(\alpha\) is finite on every \(P_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha^Tx\le\beta\) is valid for \(\bigcup_{i=1}^kP_i\) if and only if suitable \(\lambda_i\ge0\) exist for every \(i\).

notation.meaning: nonnegative validity multipliers for alternative i
coefficients of the candidate valid inequality

children.title: Disjunctive Primal–Dual Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Connections between union geometry and dual certificate systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Disjunctive Primal–Dual Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Support-function duality for a finite union of polyhedra.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(U=\bigcup_{i=1}^kP_i\), where \(P_i=\{x:A_i x\le b_i\}\) are nonempty polyhedra, and fix \(\alpha\) whose support value is finite on every alternative. Then
\[\sup_{x\in\operatorname{conv}(U)}\alpha^Tx=\max_{1\le i\le k}\sup_{x\in P_i}\alpha^Tx=\max_{1\le i\le k}\min_{\lambda_i\ge0}\{b_i^T\lambda_i:A_i^T\lambda_i=\alpha\}.\]
Thus primal optimization over the disjunctive hull corresponds to selecting the largest alternative support value, while dual feasible multipliers generate a common supporting inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The support value of a disjunctive hull is the maximum support value of its alternatives, each of which has a linear-programming multiplier dual.
assumptions_latex: All alternative support problems in direction \(\alpha\) have finite optimal values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sigma_{\operatorname{conv}(U)}(\alpha)=\max_i\min\{b_i^T\lambda_i:A_i^T\lambda_i=\alpha,\lambda_i\ge0\}\).

children.title: Hull-Membership Certificates
children.top_down_role: Certificates establishing membership in an extended or projected union hull.

knowledge_statements.title: Hull-Membership Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Homogenized extended certificate for membership in a polyhedral union hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P_i=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:A_i x\le b_i\}\) be nonempty polyhedra and \(U=\bigcup_{i=1}^kP_i\). A certificate that \(\bar x\in\operatorname{conv}(U)\) consists of vectors \(x_i\) and scalars \(\theta_i\) satisfying
\[\bar x=\sum_{i=1}^k x_i,\qquad \sum_{i=1}^k\theta_i=1,\qquad A_i x_i\le b_i\theta_i,\qquad \theta_i\ge0.\]
These linear relations are directly verifiable. Conversely, every hull member admits such a certificate; components with \(\theta_i>0\) correspond to points \(x_i/\theta_i\in P_i\), while zero-weight components account for recession directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hull membership is certified by decomposing the point into homogenized alternative components whose nonnegative weights sum to one and satisfy each scaled alternative system.
assumptions_latex: The union contains finitely many nonempty polyhedra.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x\in\operatorname{conv}(U)\) if and only if the displayed extended certificate exists.

notation.meaning: homogenized component assigned to alternative i
nonnegative convex weight of alternative i

children.title: Separating-Inequality Certificates
children.top_down_role: Certificates separating points from disjunctive hulls.

knowledge_statements.title: Separating-Inequality Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplier-verifiable strict separation from a polyhedral disjunctive hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(U=\bigcup_{i=1}^kP_i\), where \(P_i=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:A_i x\le b_i\}\) are nonempty polyhedra, and assume that \(\operatorname{conv}(U)\) is closed. For \(\bar x\notin\operatorname{conv}(U)\), a separating-inequality certificate consists of \((\alpha,\beta)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}\) and multipliers \(\lambda_i\ge0\) satisfying
\[A_i^T\lambda_i=\alpha,
\qquad b_i^T\lambda_i\le\beta\quad(i=1,\ldots,k),
\qquad \alpha^T\bar x>\beta.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point outside a closed polyhedral union hull has a violated separating inequality whose validity on every alternative is certified by nonnegative multipliers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha^Tx\le\beta<\alpha^T\bar x\) separates \(\bar x\) from \(\operatorname{conv}(U)\).

children.title: Certificate Normalization Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Normalization families used to select and stabilize dual certificates.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Normalization Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-homogeneous normalization of nonzero separating certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose a certificate system is a cone: whenever \(c=(\alpha,\beta,\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_k)\) is feasible, so is \(tc\) for every \(t>0\). Let \(g\) be continuous and positively homogeneous, with \(g(c)>0\) for every nonzero feasible certificate. The normalization interface
\[g(c)=1\]
selects one scale from each positive ray without changing the represented inequality. Standard choices include \(\|(\alpha,\beta)\|_1=1\), \(\|(\alpha,\beta)\|_2=1\), or \(\sum_i\mathbf{1}^T\lambda_i=1\), provided the chosen gauge is positive on every admissible nonzero ray.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive homogeneous gauge equal to one removes certificate scaling ambiguity, provided the gauge is strictly positive on every nonzero feasible certificate ray.
assumptions_latex: The unnormalized certificate system is invariant under positive scaling.
The selected gauge is positive on every nonzero feasible certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g(c)=1\) intersects every positive feasible certificate ray exactly once.

children.title: Split Rank Interface
children.top_down_role: Navigation to rank notions based on repeated split strengthening.

knowledge_statements.title: Split Rank Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank induced by repeated split-closure application.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a rational polyhedron \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) with integer-designated index set \(I\), a split disjunction has the form \(\pi^Tx\le\pi_0\) or \(\pi^Tx\ge\pi_0+1\), where \(\pi\in\mathbb{Z}^n\), \(\pi_j=0\) for \(j\notin I\), and \(\pi_0\in\mathbb{Z}\). Let \(S(P)\) be the intersection, over all such splits, of
\[\operatorname{conv}\bigl((P\cap\{\pi^Tx\le\pi_0\})\cup(P\cap\{\pi^Tx\ge\pi_0+1\})\bigr).\]
Define \(S^0(P)=P\) and \(S^{t+1}(P)=S(S^t(P))\). The split rank of a valid inequality is the least \(t\) for which it is valid on \(S^t(P)\), or \(+\infty\) if none exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Split rank is the minimum number of repeated split-closure rounds needed to make a target valid inequality hold, with infinite rank when no finite round suffices.
assumptions_latex: The set of integer-designated coordinates \(I\) is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}_{\mathrm{split}}(a^Tx\le b)=\min\{t\ge0:a^Tx\le b\text{ is valid on }S^t(P)\}\).

children.title: General Disjunctive Rank Interface
children.top_down_role: Navigation to rank notions based on broader disjunctive families.

knowledge_statements.title: General Disjunctive Rank Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines rank through iteration of a closure induced by an admissible family of finite disjunctions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a rational polyhedron and let \(\Delta\) be a family of finite disjunctions \(D=(D_1,\ldots,D_m)\) valid for the intended integer set. Define
\[\mathcal C_\Delta(P)=\bigcap_{D\in\Delta}\operatorname{conv}\!\left(P\cap\bigcup_{j=1}^m D_j\right),\qquad P^{(0)}=P,\quad P^{(t+1)}=\mathcal C_\Delta(P^{(t)}).\]
For a valid inequality \(a^\top x\leq\beta\), its \(\Delta\)-rank is the least \(t\in\mathbb Z_+\) for which it is valid on \(P^{(t)}\). The rank of \(P\) is the least \(t\) satisfying \(P^{(t)}=\operatorname{conv}(P\cap X_I)\), when such a finite \(t\) exists, and is \(+\infty\) otherwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A disjunctive rank counts the minimum number of closure iterations needed to obtain an inequality or the integer hull; it is infinite if no finite level suffices.
assumptions_latex: Every \(D\in\Delta\) covers the intended integer domain \(X_I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}_\Delta(a,\beta;P)=\min\{t:a^\top x\leq\beta\text{ is valid on }P^{(t)}\}\), with \(\min\varnothing=+\infty\).

children.title: Rank-Family Comparison Boundary
children.top_down_role: Scope boundary for comparisons between split-specific and general disjunctive ranks.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Family Comparison Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies sufficient conditions under which closure dominance yields a rank comparison and why family names or initial-level inclusion alone do not.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal C_F\) and \(\mathcal C_G\) be closure operators on relaxations containing a common target \(H\). Define \(F^0(P)=G^0(P)=P\), \(F^{t+1}(P)=\mathcal C_F(F^t(P))\), and \(G^{t+1}(P)=\mathcal C_G(G^t(P))\). Assume \(H\subseteq\mathcal C_F(Q)\subseteq Q\) and \(H\subseteq\mathcal C_G(Q)\subseteq Q\) for every relevant relaxation \(Q\), that \(\mathcal C_G\) is monotone under set inclusion, and that
\[\mathcal C_F(Q)\subseteq\mathcal C_G(Q)\]
for every relaxation reachable by either hierarchy. Then \(F^t(P)\subseteq G^t(P)\) for every \(t\in\mathbb Z_+\), and
\[\operatorname{rank}_F(P)\leq\operatorname{rank}_G(P),\]
where each rank is the least level attaining \(H\), with value \(+\infty\) if no such level exists. Inclusion only at \(P\), or inclusion restricted to a subclass not containing all relevant iterates, does not establish this global rank ordering. Without uniform dominance on the relevant class, no rank-family comparison follows without additional hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform closure dominance over all relevant iterates, together with the needed monotonicity, implies rank dominance. Initial-level or subclass-specific inclusion alone does not compare entire rank families.
assumptions_latex: \(F^0(P)=G^0(P)=P\), and both hierarchies retain the common target \(H\).
\(\mathcal C_G\) is monotone under set inclusion on the relevant relaxation class.
\(\mathcal C_F(Q)\subseteq\mathcal C_G(Q)\) holds for every relaxation reachable by either hierarchy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F^t(P)\subseteq G^t(P)\) for every \(t\in\mathbb Z_+\), and \(\operatorname{rank}_F(P)\leq\operatorname{rank}_G(P)\).

notation.meaning: The t-th iterate of closure family F from P.
The t-th iterate of closure family G from P.

children.title: Lift–Project Relaxation Families
children.top_down_role: Higher-dimensional relaxation families connected to disjunctive strengthening.

knowledge_statements.title: Lift–Project Relaxation Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Represents binary lift–project families as closures generated by variable disjunctions and projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(P\subseteq[0,1]^n\), define the elementary variable-disjunction closure
\[L_i(P)=\operatorname{conv}\bigl((P\cap\{x:x_i=0\})\cup(P\cap\{x:x_i=1\})\bigr).\]
A lift–project relaxation family constructs an extended polyhedron encoding one or more such disjunctions, applies a prescribed linear or conic lifting rule, and projects the lifted feasible region to the original \(x\)-space. The simultaneous first-level closure is
\[L(P)=\bigcap_{i=1}^n L_i(P).\]
Sequential, simultaneous, linear, and semidefinite liftings define distinct families; their relaxations must therefore be identified by both the lifting cone and the set of disjunctions imposed at each level.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lift–project families encode binary disjunctions in an extended space and project back; different lifting cones and disjunction schedules define different relaxation families.
assumptions_latex: The intended integer points satisfy \(x_i\in\{0,1\}\) for each lifted coordinate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L(P)=\bigcap_{i=1}^n\operatorname{conv}((P\cap\{x_i=0\})\cup(P\cap\{x_i=1\}))\).

notation.meaning: Closure from the binary disjunction on coordinate i.

children.title: Hierarchy Level Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Navigation across successive levels of lifted strengthening systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Hierarchy Level Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines levels independently of the particular lift, cone, or disjunction schedule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(L\) be a specified lift–project closure operator on relaxations of a target set \(H\). Its hierarchy is
\[P^{[0]}=P,
\qquad P^{[t+1]}=L(P^{[t]})\quad(t\in\mathbb Z_+).\]
A level interface must expose the index \(t\), the ambient variables before projection, the lifting cone, the disjunctions processed at that application, and the projected relaxation \(P^{[t]}\). Validity requires
\[H\subseteq P^{[t+1]}\subseteq P^{[t]}\subseteq P.\]
Finite convergence occurs at level \(r\) precisely when \(P^{[r]}=H\); absent such an index, the hierarchy has infinite convergence rank on \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hierarchy level is one specified closure application, with its lift and projection metadata; levels form nested relaxations containing the target hull.
assumptions_latex: \(L(Q)\) is defined for every hierarchy relaxation \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H\subseteq P^{[t+1]}\subseteq P^{[t]}\), and \(r=\min\{t:P^{[t]}=H\}\).

notation.meaning: Projected relaxation at hierarchy level t.
Target hull retained by every level.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Level-t Sherali–Adams relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition of hierarchy levels through bounded-degree variable and complement products.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a binary system Ax\ge b and an integer 1\le t\le n, the level-t Sherali\text{–}Adams construction multiplies Ax-b\ge0 by every product \prod_{i\in I}x_i\prod_{j\in J}(1-x_j), where I\cap J=\varnothing and 1\le |I|+|J|\le t. The resulting lift-and-project relaxation is denoted S_t, and S_1=N.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At level t, Sherali–Adams multiplies the binary linear inequalities by every product of variables and complemented variables of total degree from one through t. The resulting lift-and-project relaxation is S_t, with S1 equal to N.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S_t\text{ denotes the resulting level-}t\text{ relaxation},\qquad S_1=N.

knowledge_statements.title: Formulation–Hierarchy Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates extended-formulation strength and size from iterative hierarchy depth.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E_t=\{(x,z):A_tx+B_tz\leq b_t\}\) be an extended formulation whose projection equals a hierarchy relaxation, \(\operatorname{proj}_x(E_t)=P^{[t]}\). This equality permits comparison at the fixed level \(t\), but it does not identify formulation size with hierarchy rank: the number of inequalities or auxiliary variables in \(E_t\) is not the number of closure iterations. Moreover, a compact formulation of \(P^{[t]}\) neither implies compact formulations at other levels nor finite convergence to the target hull. Claims transferring strength across formulations require equality or inclusion after projection; comparisons made only in incompatible extended spaces are insufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An extended formulation may represent one hierarchy level, but its size is not hierarchy depth, and comparisons require projection into a common space.
assumptions_latex: \(E_t\) is an extended formulation in variables \((x,z)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_x(E_t)=P^{[t]}\) does not imply \(\operatorname{size}(E_t)=t\) or finite hierarchy convergence.

children.title: Intersection Cut Interface

knowledge_statements.title: Intersection Cut Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the ray form of an intersection cut obtained from a forbidden convex region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Q=\{\bar x+\sum_{j=1}^q r^js_j:s\in\mathbb R_+^q\}\), where \(\bar x\) lies in the interior of a closed convex set \(S\), while every feasible mixed-integer point of interest lies outside \(\operatorname{int}(S)\). For each ray define
\[\alpha_j=\sup\{\alpha\geq0:\bar x+\alpha r^j\in S\}.\]
With the convention \(1/\infty=0\), the intersection cut is
\[\sum_{j:\alpha_j>0}\frac{s_j}{\alpha_j}\geq1.\]
It is valid for the points of \(Q\) outside \(\operatorname{int}(S)\); rays with \(\alpha_j=\infty\) receive zero coefficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ray exit distances from a forbidden convex region produce a valid inequality excluding the cone apex while retaining feasible points outside the region's interior.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\) is a finitely generated translated polyhedral cone.
\(\bar x\in\operatorname{int}(S)\), and relevant feasible points avoid \(\operatorname{int}(S)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{j:\alpha_j>0}s_j/\alpha_j\geq1\) is valid for \(Q\setminus\operatorname{int}(S)\).

notation.meaning: Cone apex lying inside the forbidden region.
Extreme or generating ray of the cone.
Ray distance to the boundary of S.

children.title: Disjunctive Cut Interface
children.top_down_role: Navigation to inequalities derived directly from disjunctive structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Disjunctive Cut Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a cut by validity over every branch of a finite disjunction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and let \(D_1,\ldots,D_m\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) form a disjunction valid for the intended feasible set. An inequality \(a^\top x\leq\beta\) is a disjunctive cut for \((P,D_1,\ldots,D_m)\) when
\[a^\top x\leq\beta\quad\text{for every }x\in P\cap D_j\text{ and every }j=1,\ldots,m.\]
Equivalently, it is valid for
\[\operatorname{conv}\!\left(\bigcup_{j=1}^m(P\cap D_j)\right).\]
It cuts the current relaxation only if some point of \(P\) violates it; branchwise validity, rather than mere validity on one branch, is the defining certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A disjunctive cut is valid on every branch intersection and hence on their convex hull; it is separating only when the original relaxation violates it.
assumptions_latex: The branch union \(\bigcup_{j=1}^mD_j\) contains the intended feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a^\top x\leq\beta\) is valid for \(\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_{j=1}^m(P\cap D_j))\).

notation.meaning: Branch set of the finite disjunction.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 2. The Convex Hull of a Disjunctive Set p. 17

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 2. The Convex Hull of a Disjunctive Set p. 17

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sufficient Multiplier Certificate for a Binary Split Inequality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The extract supplies a sufficient certificate for the two sets P^0 and P^1 under consideration but does not restate their definitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the disjunctive sets P^0 and P^1 under consideration, the inequality \gamma x\leq\gamma_0 is valid for \operatorname{conv}(P^0\cup P^1) if there exist u^i\in\mathbb{R}_+^m, v^i\in\mathbb{R}_+^n, and w^i\in\mathbb{R}_+ for i=0,1 such that
\[\gamma\leq u^0A+v^0+w^0e_j,\qquad \gamma\leq u^1A+v^1-w^1e_j,\]
\[\gamma_0\geq u^0b+\mathbf{1}\cdot v^0,\qquad \gamma_0\geq u^1b+\mathbf{1}\cdot v^1-w^1.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the stated binary disjunction, nonnegative multipliers satisfying the displayed coefficient and right-hand-side bounds certify that the proposed inequality is valid for the convex hull of the two terms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \gamma x\leq\gamma_0\text{ is valid for }\operatorname{conv}(P^0\cup P^1).

children.title: Cut-Family Overlap
children.top_down_role: Shared scope and distinctions between intersection-based and disjunction-based cuts.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Family Overlap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies the standard overlap between polyhedral intersection cuts and finite disjunctive cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[S=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:d_k^\top x\leq\delta_k,\ k=1,\ldots,\ell\}\]
be a closed polyhedron, and let the cone apex \(\bar x\) lie in \(\operatorname{int}(S)\). Then
\[\mathbb R^n\setminus\operatorname{int}(S)=\bigcup_{k=1}^{\ell}\{x\in\mathbb R^n:d_k^\top x\geq\delta_k\}.\]
For a translated polyhedral cone \(Q\) with apex \(\bar x\), let \(\iota_{S,Q}\) denote the intersection-cut inequality obtained from the first exit of each generating ray from \(S\). The inequality \(\iota_{S,Q}\) is valid on every branch of the displayed disjunction and hence belongs to its disjunctive-cut family. Thus intersection cuts derived from polyhedral forbidden regions overlap the finite disjunctive-cut family. This statement does not identify the full families when forbidden regions are nonpolyhedral or when a disjunction is not representable as the exterior of one common convex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a polyhedral forbidden region, its exterior is a finite facet disjunction, and the associated intersection-cut inequality belongs to the corresponding disjunctive-cut family. The broader families need not coincide.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is a closed polyhedron with \(\bar x\in\operatorname{int}(S)\).
\(Q\) is a translated polyhedral cone with apex \(\bar x\).
\(\iota_{S,Q}\) uses the first exit distances of the generating rays from \(S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\iota_{S,Q}\in\mathcal D(\bigvee_{k=1}^{\ell}\{x:d_k^\top x\geq\delta_k\},Q)\).

notation.meaning: Translated polyhedral cone whose apex lies inside S.
Intersection-cut inequality associated with S and Q.
Family of inequalities valid branchwise for the specified disjunction on Q.

children.title: Automatic Reformulation Interfaces

children.title: Automatic Big-M Transformation
children.top_down_role: Generation and validation of bound-dependent activation formulations.

knowledge_statements.title: Automatic Big-M Transformation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compiles branch constraints using validated finite upper bounds on their possible violations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input a bounded domain \(X\), branch systems \(g_{kj}(x)\leq0\), and selectors \(y_k\in\{0,1\}\) with \(\sum_{k=1}^m y_k=1\). For each branch constraint compute or certify
\[M_{kj}\geq\sup_{x\in X}g_{kj}(x),\qquad M_{kj}<+\infty.\]
Emit
\[g_{kj}(x)\leq M_{kj}(1-y_k)\quad(k=1,\ldots,m),
\qquad \sum_{k=1}^m y_k=1.\]
When \(y_k=1\), branch \(k\)'s constraints are enforced; when \(y_k=0\), their certified bounds make them redundant on \(X\). Reject or defer any constraint lacking a finite valid bound, and output the transformed model together with its bound certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compute finite violation bounds, emit selector-controlled constraints, and reject transformations whose deactivated constraints lack valid finite bounds.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is the domain used to validate every bound.
Each accepted \(M_{kj}\) is finite and dominates \(g_{kj}\) on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g_{kj}(x)\leq M_{kj}(1-y_k)\) enforces branch \(k\) exactly when \(y_k=1\) and is redundant on \(X\) when \(y_k=0\).

notation.meaning: Certified upper bound on constraint violation.
