children.title: Automatic Hull Transformation
children.top_down_role: Generation of disaggregated and perspective-based hull formulations.

knowledge_statements.title: Automatic Hull Transformation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Builds a disaggregated extended formulation whose projection is the convex hull of a finite polyhedral union.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input nonempty bounded polyhedra \(P_k=\{x:A_kx\leq b_k\}\) for \(k=1,\ldots,m\). Introduce disaggregated variables \(x^k\) and selectors \(y_k\), and emit
\[x=\sum_{k=1}^m x^k,
\qquad A_kx^k\leq b_ky_k,
\qquad \sum_{k=1}^m y_k=1,
\qquad y_k\geq0.\]
For an exact mixed-integer disjunction, additionally impose \(y_k\in\{0,1\}\). The continuous selector formulation projects to \(\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_{k=1}^mP_k)\); binary selectors select one branch. An implementation must preserve scaled variable bounds or use the appropriate homogenized branch formulation when branch descriptions have nontrivial recession directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Disaggregate variables by branch, scale each branch system by its selector, and recombine them; projection yields the convex hull of a bounded polyhedral union.
assumptions_latex: Each \(P_k=\{x:A_kx\leq b_k\}\) is nonempty and bounded.
The branch descriptions are used in their scaled homogeneous form.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\(\operatorname{proj}_x\{(x,x^k,y):x=\sum_kx^k,
\ A_kx^k\leq b_ky_k,
\ y\geq0,
\ \sum_ky_k=1\}=\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_kP_k)\).

children.title: Mixed Transformation Selection
children.top_down_role: Per-construct selection among compact, extended, and native representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed Transformation Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selects eligible representations per construct while enforcing compatibility across shared model structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For logical constructs \(c\in C\), let \(R_c\) contain candidate representations such as native, big-M, or hull forms. Compute eligibility predicates \(E(c,r)\in\{0,1\}\) from solver support, finite-bound availability, convexity, and branch structure. Given a declared cost score \(w(c,r)\), select
\[r^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{r_c\in R_c}\sum_{c\in C}w(c,r_c)\]
subject to \(E(c,r_c)=1\) for every \(c\) and all compatibility constraints induced by shared variables or nested logic. Emit the conjunction of the selected transformations plus their validation certificates. If no feasible selection exists, return an eligibility diagnostic instead of silently weakening or dropping a construct.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose an eligible representation for each logical construct by a stated cost rule, respect cross-construct compatibility, and report failure when no valid combination exists.
assumptions_latex: Each candidate representation has a sound eligibility test.
The cost score and compatibility constraints are fixed before selection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r^*\) minimizes the declared score over all eligible, mutually compatible transformation assignments.

source_refs.locator: 4.5.1 A Disjunctive Programming Formulation p. 64
4.5.2 A Tighter Disjunctive Programming Formulation p. 65

source_witnesses.locator: 4.5.1 A Disjunctive Programming Formulation p. 64
4.5.2 A Tighter Disjunctive Programming Formulation p. 65

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited formulation sections may support big-M and hull representations, but they do not establish the proposed global cost-minimizing selection algorithm, its eligibility predicates, or compatibility model. A source specifically supporting automatic mixed-reformulation selection is required.

children.title: Reformulation Eligibility Validation
children.top_down_role: Modeling-system checks for finite bounds, logical consistency, and reformulation eligibility.

children.title: Finite-Bound Validation
children.top_down_role: Checks concerning availability and suitability of finite variable bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Bound Validation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives the necessary bound certificate for safely deactivating a constraint by a big-M term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a conditional constraint \(g(x)\leq0\) over validation domain \(X\), a proposed upper big-M constant \(M\in\mathbb R\) passes finite-bound validation exactly when
\[M<+\infty
\quad\text{and}\quad
\sup_{x\in X}g(x)\leq M.\]
For a linear row \(a^\top x\leq b\) with box bounds \(\ell_i\leq x_i\leq u_i\), the tight box-derived certificate is
\[M^*=\sum_{i:a_i>0}a_iu_i+
\sum_{i:a_i<0}a_i\ell_i-b,\]
provided every bound used with a nonzero coefficient is finite. Missing relevant bounds, an unbounded validation problem, or a value below the certified supremum makes the transformation ineligible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A deactivation constant is valid only if finite and at least the maximum constraint violation over the declared domain; linear box bounds give an explicit certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is the complete domain applicable while the constraint is inactive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\) is valid if and only if \(M\in\mathbb R\) and \(M\geq\sup_{x\in X}g(x)\).

notation.meaning: Domain on which deactivation must be safe.
Tight bound derived from the stated variable box.

children.title: Structural Eligibility Validation
children.top_down_role: Checks that modeled constructs meet the structural requirements of a reformulation.

assumptions_latex: The source model has finitely many declared variables, constraints, logical operators, and disjunctions.
Every reformulation template declares the syntactic and domain conditions under which it is applicable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A reformulation is structurally eligible exactly when every expression and logical construct is accepted by its selected template and all required incidence restrictions hold.

notation.meaning: structural acceptance predicate for template t

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Template-relative structural validation before automatic reformulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C(M)\) be the finite set of reformulable constructs in a model \(M\), and let \(t(c)\) be the template selected for \(c\in C(M)\). Structural eligibility is the predicate \[E(M):=\bigwedge_{c\in C(M)}E_{t(c)}(c),\] where \(E_t(c)\) asserts that \(c\) has an operator type, variable domains, argument dimensions, and incidence pattern admitted by template \(t\). The model passes structural validation if and only if \(E(M)\) is true. This test concerns representability by the templates; it does not establish finite coefficient bounds or logical consistency.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A model is structurally eligible when every targeted construct satisfies the type, domain, dimension, and incidence requirements of its selected reformulation template.
knowledge_statements.title: Structural Eligibility Validation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the Structural Eligibility Validation leaf and is internally coherent, but it is a template-relative interface specification rather than a source-supported standard result. No source_ref or inspectable locator establishes the stated eligibility fields or biconditional.

children.title: Logical Consistency Screening
children.top_down_role: Screening for incompatible or incomplete logical alternatives.

assumptions_latex: The propositional abstraction contains finitely many Boolean atoms and clauses.
Any theory-dependent implications used by the screen are valid for the declared variable domains.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Unsatisfiability certifies logical inconsistency; satisfiability provides a logically admissible assignment but does not by itself certify numerical feasibility.

notation.meaning: propositional abstraction of the model logic

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite propositional screening augmented by sound domain implications.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a model, introduce one Boolean atom for each primitive logical condition and compile its connectives, implications, and exactly-one requirements into a finite formula \(\Phi\). Add a finite set \(T\) of sound clauses implied by declared domains, fixed variables, and mutually exclusive alternatives. Invoke a satisfiability procedure on \(\Phi\land\bigwedge_{	au\in T}\tau\). If it is unsatisfiable, return the contradictory clause core when available and reject the reformulation as logically inconsistent. If it is satisfiable, return an assignment to the atoms and pass the logical screen, without claiming feasibility of the associated numerical constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compile the model logic with sound domain implications and run a satisfiability check; contradiction rejects the reformulation, while satisfiability passes only the logical screen.
knowledge_statements.title: Logical Consistency Screening

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is the appropriate content kind, and the distinction between propositional satisfiability and numerical feasibility is sound. However, no cited source supports the compilation scheme, theory-clause assumptions, or contradictory-core behavior.

children.title: Reformulation Failure Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Diagnostic categories for models that cannot safely enter an automatic transformation.

assumptions_latex: Each validation rule has a stable identifier and an explicitly declared applicability predicate.
The validator records the source construct and template involved in every failed rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned diagnostic is a verifiable witness that at least one necessary reformulation condition failed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Machine-checkable diagnostics for rejected automatic reformulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a source model \(M\), construct \(c\), and proposed template \(t\), a reformulation-failure diagnostic is a tuple \(d=(r,c,t,w)\), where \(r\in R\) identifies a necessary validation rule and \(w\) contains the data needed to evaluate its predicate. The tuple is valid when \[\neg P_r(M,c,t)\] can be recomputed from \(w\) and the declarations of \(M\). A diagnostic may identify, for example, an unsupported operator, incompatible domain, missing finite bound, dimension mismatch, or contradictory logical requirement. Validation failure must return at least one valid tuple and must not report successful reformulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A failure diagnostic identifies a violated necessary rule, the offending construct and template, and enough model data to recompute the violation.
knowledge_statements.title: Reformulation Failure Diagnostics

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A certificate is a defensible kind for a machine-checkable failure diagnostic, but the tuple schema, recomputability requirement, and mandatory return behavior are interface-specific and have no cited evidence.

children.title: Solver-Native Logical Processing
children.top_down_role: Retention of high-level constraint identity for solver-specific inference and search.

children.title: Logical Inference Calculus
children.top_down_role: Domain inference and simplification driven by logical structure.

children.title: Logical Presolve
children.top_down_role: Structure-aware simplification performed before or during solver processing.

assumptions_latex: The logical model is finite and every applied inference rule preserves its set of feasible assignments.
Assignments and clauses are represented exactly at the logical level.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is logically equivalent to the input on retained variables, or infeasibility is correctly certified.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence-preserving presolve for finite logical models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \((F_0,a_0)\) with the model's logical constraints and declared fixed truth values. Repeatedly apply sound rules: remove satisfied clauses, delete falsified literals, propagate unit clauses, substitute equivalent literals, eliminate duplicate or subsumed clauses, and detect violated empty clauses. Stop when a fixed point is reached or an empty clause is produced. In the first case, output \((F_*,a_*)\) together with a reconstruction map such that every solution of \(F_*\) extends to a solution of \(F_0\), and every solution of \(F_0\) restricts to one of \(F_*\). In the second case, output infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Logical presolve repeatedly simplifies clauses and fixes implied truth values while preserving reconstructible solutions, stopping at a fixed point or a contradiction.
knowledge_statements.title: Logical Presolve

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm matches Logical Presolve and states an appropriate reconstruction invariant. No authoritative source or locator supports the selected rule set and the claimed bidirectional solution correspondence.

children.title: Domain Propagation
children.top_down_role: Domain inference driven by conditional, disjunctive, or ordered structure.

assumptions_latex: Each constraint propagator is sound for the current variable domains.
Every domain is represented by bounds or a finite value set supporting intersection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every removed value is infeasible relative to a processed constraint and the current domains; an empty domain certifies infeasibility.

notation.meaning: sound filtering operator for constraint c

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound fixed-point filtering of logical and numerical domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(D_i^0\) to the declared domain of each variable \(x_i\). For every constraint \(c\), a sound propagator \(P_c\) returns domains satisfying \[P_c(D^k)_i\subseteq D_i^k\quad\text{and}\quad \{x_i:x\in c,\ x_j\in D_j^k\ \forall j\}\subseteq P_c(D^k)_i.\] Apply propagators whenever an incident domain changes, intersecting their outputs with the current domains. Stop when no domain changes, and return the fixed-point domains. If some \(D_i^k=\varnothing\), return infeasible. Otherwise, the reduced domains retain every solution contained in the initial domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sound constraint propagators repeatedly remove unsupported domain values until reaching a fixed point; an empty domain certifies infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Domain Propagation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm belongs in Domain Propagation, but the displayed support set uses the ill-typed expression x in c, where c was introduced as a constraint rather than a set. Moreover, bounds over nonfinite domains do not by themselves guarantee finite fixed-point termination. A source is needed to determine the intended propagator invariant and termination model.

children.title: Presolve–Propagation Feedback
children.top_down_role: Interactions through which simplification enables further domain inference.

assumptions_latex: Every presolve transformation has a valid reconstruction map or preserves the retained solution set directly.
Every propagation step is sound for the currently transformed model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Termination returns a mutually stable reduced model and domains preserving all original solutions, or a sound infeasibility certificate.

notation.meaning: variable domains after outer iteration k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Alternating presolve and propagation to mutual stability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \((M_0,D^0)\) from the source model. At outer iteration \(k\), run sound presolve on \((M_k,D^k)\) to obtain \(\widehat M_k\) and possibly tighter domains \(\widehat D^k\); then propagate all constraints of \(\widehat M_k\) to a domain fixed point \(D^{k+1}\), producing \(M_{k+1}=\widehat M_k\). Requeue presolve whenever propagation fixes a variable or changes a domain in a way that enables a presolve rule. Stop when neither phase changes the represented model or domains, or when either phase certifies infeasibility. Output the reduced model, domains, and composed reconstruction map.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternate sound presolve and domain propagation, reactivating either phase after relevant changes, until mutual stability or certified infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Presolve–Propagation Feedback

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The alternating algorithm fits Presolve–Propagation Feedback, but finite termination is not implied by the assumptions: domain tightening can generate an infinite descending sequence. A cited finite-representation, tolerance, or strict-progress rule is required.

children.title: Structure-Aware Branching Family
children.top_down_role: Structure-aware branching interfaces for conditional and ordered alternatives.

children.title: Indicator Branching
children.top_down_role: Branching interfaces that exploit conditional activation structure.

assumptions_latex: The current node relaxation admits a solution with a fractional indicator variable.
Each indicator variable is required to be binary in integer-feasible solutions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The two children cover all integer-feasible solutions of the parent and exclude the selected fractional relaxation point.

notation.meaning: binary indicator for a conditional constraint
current relaxation value of the indicator

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary branching on a fractional logical indicator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a branch-and-bound node, solve the current relaxation and identify indicators satisfying \(0<\bar z_j<1\). Select one such indicator \(z_j\) using a declared score, such as pseudocost or estimated bound improvement. Create two child nodes by imposing, respectively, \(z_j=0\) and \(z_j=1\), and activate or deactivate the associated conditional constraints according to their declared semantics. Propagate both children and discard any child proved infeasible. Because integer-feasible points require \(z_j\in\{0,1\}\), the children partition the parent's integer-feasible solutions and the current fractional point belongs to neither child.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose a fractional binary indicator and create children fixing it to zero and one, then enforce the corresponding conditional semantics and propagate.
knowledge_statements.title: Indicator Branching

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The binary split is mathematically valid and the algorithm kind fits Indicator Branching. Evidence is still required for the solver-native activation/deactivation semantics and candidate-selection behavior; no source_ref is supplied.

children.title: SOS Branching
children.top_down_role: Branching interfaces specialized for special ordered sets.

assumptions_latex: The ordered variables form an SOS1 or SOS2 set with declared nonnegative weights or activity variables.
The current relaxation violates the applicable special-ordered-set support restriction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The children cover every SOS-feasible support pattern while excluding the selected violating relaxation support.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Support branching for SOS1 and SOS2 constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((x_1,\ldots,x_m)\) be ordered. For SOS1, choose \(p\) separating positive relaxation activity and create children imposing \(x_i=0\) for all \(i>p\) and \(x_i=0\) for all \(i\le p\), respectively. For SOS2, choose an adjacent split and create children whose permitted nonzero indices lie, respectively, in \(\{1,\ldots,p+1\}\) and \(\{p,\ldots,m\}\). Select \(p\) so the current violating support is cut off. Propagate each child. Every support satisfying the original SOS restriction is retained in at least one child.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Split an ordered SOS support into two admissible index regions so all SOS-feasible patterns remain covered while the current violating support is removed.
knowledge_statements.title: SOS Branching

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm combines SOS1 and SOS2 rules without separately defining their support restrictions, ordering data, and split-selection conditions. The claim that a suitable p cuts off the current support therefore cannot be checked from the record, and no source resolves the variant-specific semantics.

children.title: Disjunction Branching
children.top_down_role: Branching interfaces based directly on alternative disjunctive regimes.

assumptions_latex: Every integer-feasible point at the current node satisfies a finite disjunction.
The current relaxation point violates every term of that disjunction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The child union contains every integer-feasible parent solution and excludes the current relaxation point.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Branching directly on a valid finite disjunction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a node with relaxation region \(P\), select a valid finite disjunction \[Q_1\lor\cdots\lor Q_q\] satisfied by every integer-feasible point in \(P\), but by no term at the current relaxation point \(\bar x\). Create child \(r\) with relaxation region \(P_r=P\cap Q_r\) for each \(r\in\{1,\ldots,q\}\), then propagate and discard infeasible children. The branching rule is complete because every integer-feasible point of the parent lies in at least one \(P_r\). It is separating because \(\bar x\notin\bigcup_{r=1}^qP_r\). Overlap between children is permitted unless a partition is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Create one child for each term of a valid disjunction that covers all integer-feasible points but excludes the current relaxation point.
knowledge_statements.title: Disjunction Branching

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-disjunction branching rule is precise, has the correct algorithm kind, and correctly distinguishes coverage from partition. It nevertheless has no citation or inspectable locator, and the supplied local inventory does not document this branching result.

children.title: Branching Regime Selection
children.top_down_role: Structural criteria governing the choice among native branching interfaces.

assumptions_latex: Each eligible branching candidate generates children covering all integer-feasible solutions of the current node.
Candidate scores use only information available at the node or valid historical estimates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected regime maximizes the declared score among eligible candidates without compromising branching validity.

notation.meaning: eligible branching candidates at node N

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Node-local selection among valid structure-aware branching regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At node \(N\), construct the finite eligible set \(\mathcal B(N)\) of indicator, SOS, and general disjunction branches. Remove any candidate whose children fail coverage of the node's integer-feasible set. For each remaining \(b\), compute a declared score \(S_N(b)\) from predicted child-bound improvements, balance, propagation gain, and estimated processing cost; unavailable estimates may be obtained by bounded strong-branching trials. Select \[b^*\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{b\in\mathcal B(N)}S_N(b),\] apply its children, and update historical estimates from observed outcomes. If \(\mathcal B(N)=\varnothing\), defer to a valid fallback integer branching rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Filter for valid candidate branches, score eligible indicator, SOS, and disjunction regimes by predicted benefit and cost, and apply a maximizing candidate.
knowledge_statements.title: Branching Regime Selection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is the correct role for Branching Regime Selection, and filtering candidates for coverage preserves validity. The proposed composite score, bounded strong-branching estimates, and fallback policy are solver-dependent and unsupported by any cited source.

children.title: Logical Conflict Analysis
children.top_down_role: Conflict and infeasibility information retaining logical participation.

assumptions_latex: The conflicting node state was derived by sound logical inference from finite clauses and branching decisions.
Each recorded implication names antecedent literals sufficient for its consequent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The learned clause is valid for the original model, excludes the conflicting assignment, and can participate in later propagation.

notation.meaning: set of literals assigned true in the conflict explanation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clause learning from sound logical implication records.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose sound implication records show that the simultaneous truth of a finite set of literals \(A=\{\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_k\}\) entails contradiction. The clause \[C:=\neg\ell_1\lor\cdots\lor\neg\ell_k\] is then a logical conflict certificate. It is verifiable by replaying the recorded implications from \(A\) to the contradictory state. Conflict analysis may resolve this clause with recorded reason clauses to remove nondecision literals, provided every resolution step is logged. The resulting learned clause must be implied by the original model and must retain the involved indicator or logical literals so that it can propagate at later search nodes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replayable implication records justify a learned clause that excludes the conflicting logical assignment and preserves participating literals for future propagation.
knowledge_statements.title: Logical Conflict Analysis

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The learned clause can serve as a certificate, but the exact terminal is Logical Conflict Analysis, for which the whole record is principally an analysis/learning algorithm rather than merely a certificate. The requirement that the final clause retain involved logical literals is not a general consequence of resolution and needs a source or narrower semantics.

children.title: Tolerance-Aware Logical Semantics
children.top_down_role: Solver interpretation of activity, zero values, and logical feasibility under tolerances.

assumptions_latex: The solver declares nonnegative integrality, feasibility, and activity tolerances.
All logical tests use the same declared tolerance policy or an explicitly documented stronger policy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Logical truth, zero activity, and constraint feasibility are determined by the displayed tolerance predicates rather than exact floating-point equality.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit numerical predicates for solver-native logical interpretation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a nominally binary variable \(z\), define logical false when \(|z|\le\varepsilon_I\), logical true when \(|z-1|\le\varepsilon_I\), and logically indeterminate otherwise. Define a numerical activity \(x
e 0\) to be treated as zero when \(|x|\le\varepsilon_Z\). A row \(g(x)\le 0\) is feasibility-satisfied when \(g(x)\le\varepsilon_F\), and \(g(x)=0\) is feasibility-satisfied when \(|g(x)|\le\varepsilon_F\). Indicator activation and logical feasibility must be evaluated using these predicates. Values satisfying both competing predicates, if tolerances overlap, require a declared deterministic tie rule rather than inconsistent truth assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solver-native logic interprets binary truth, zero activity, and row feasibility through declared tolerances, with a deterministic rule for any overlapping classifications.
knowledge_statements.title: Tolerance-Aware Logical Semantics

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Definition is an appropriate content kind for this leaf, but the predicates are a proposed solver policy rather than universal logical semantics. Nonnegative integrality tolerance permits overlapping true and false neighborhoods, and the unspecified tie rule does not define the resulting truth value. Solver documentation with a precise policy and locator is required.

children.title: Logic-Based Outer Approximation Interface

knowledge_statements.title: Logic-Based Outer Approximation Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interface contract for convex logic-based outer approximation with discrete master decisions and continuous subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a finite logical assignment set \(Y\), solve at iteration \(k\) a master problem over \(y\in Y\) and an epigraph variable \(\eta\), subject to accumulated valid inequalities \(\eta\geq \ell_t(y)\). For a selected assignment \(y^k\), solve the associated convex continuous subproblem. If it is feasible, return its value \(v(y^k)\), an optimizer, and a valid supporting underestimator \(\ell_k\) satisfying \(\ell_k(y)\leq v(y)\) for every \(y\in Y\). If it is infeasible, return a valid logical or convex feasibility cut excluding \(y^k\). Stop when the incumbent upper bound minus the master lower bound is at most \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The master selects a logical assignment; its continuous subproblem returns an objective cut or feasibility cut until the certified bound gap meets tolerance.
assumptions_latex: Every feasible subproblem is convex and solved globally.
Returned cuts are valid for all assignments in \(Y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At termination, the incumbent has certified absolute optimality gap at most \(\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: Optimal value of the continuous subproblem fixed at assignment y.
Valid master underestimator generated at iteration k.

children.title: Logical Alternative Branching
children.top_down_role: Branching over explicit logical alternatives within a search framework.

knowledge_statements.title: Logical Alternative Branching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exhaustive branching on a finite disjunction at a search-tree node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a node with current feasible set \(F\), choose a finite exhaustive disjunction \(D_1\vee\cdots\vee D_m\) that is valid on \(F\), meaning \(F\subseteq\bigcup_{j=1}^m D_j\). Create child \(j\) with feasible set \(F_j=F\cap D_j\), and discard any child proved empty. If the alternatives overlap, impose a fixed priority rule or additional negations to obtain disjoint children when unique assignment of feasible points is required. The union of the retained children equals \(F\), so branching neither removes a feasible solution nor introduces one outside the parent set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Branching intersects the parent feasible set with every alternative of a valid exhaustive disjunction, preserving the parent set as the children’s union.
assumptions_latex: The chosen disjunction is valid for the parent feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F=\bigcup_{j=1}^m F_j\), where \(F_j=F\cap D_j\).

notation.meaning: Logical alternative used for child j.

children.title: Node-Level Logical Inference
children.top_down_role: Logical deductions associated with individual search nodes.

knowledge_statements.title: Node-Level Logical Inference
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound propagation of Boolean and disjunctive restrictions at one search node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L\) be the node's current set of fixed literals and let \(\Phi\) be a finite logical theory. Repeatedly apply sound implication rules of the form \(P\Rightarrow q\): whenever every literal in premise \(P\) is entailed by \(L\), add conclusion \(q\) to \(L\). Stop at a fixed point, or fathom the node if both \(q\) and \(\neg q\) are derived for some proposition. Because every rule is valid for \(\Phi\), the fixed-point literals are consequences of \(\Phi\wedge\bigwedge L_0\), where \(L_0\) denotes the initial node literals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sound implication rules propagate node fixings to closure; deriving a literal and its negation certifies node infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(\Phi\) and the implication-rule collection are finite.
Every applied implication rule is valid for \(\Phi\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure terminates; every derived literal is entailed by \(\Phi\wedge\bigwedge L_0\), and a derived contradiction certifies infeasibility.

notation.meaning: Initial literals fixed at the search node.
Sound inference rule with conjunctive premise P.

children.title: Search-Tree Structure Interface

knowledge_statements.title: Search-Tree Structure Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-theoretic interface between logical branching and a rooted search tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent a search tree by a rooted directed tree \(T=(V,E)\). Associate the root with the original feasible set \(F_r\). For every internal node \(u\), a branching oracle returns children \(C(u)\) and restrictions whose feasible sets satisfy \(F_v\subseteq F_u\) for all \(v\in C(u)\) and \(F_u=\bigcup_{v\in C(u)}F_v\). A node may be fathomed only by a valid infeasibility certificate, a valid bound relative to the incumbent, or completion of its optimization. Consequently, every feasible solution not yet certified suboptimal belongs to at least one active leaf.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each tree node carries a restricted feasible set; exhaustive children cover their parent, and only certified pruning may remove a branch.
assumptions_latex: Each branching operation is finite and exhaustive.
Every fathoming decision has a valid certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every unresolved feasible point in \(F_r\) lies in the feasible set of at least one active leaf.

notation.meaning: Feasible set represented by node u.

children.title: Algorithmic Delegation Boundary
children.top_down_role: Boundary between formulation interfaces and full branch-bound algorithm theory.

knowledge_statements.title: Algorithmic Delegation Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal correctness contract for delegating logical branching to a search engine.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A formulation layer may delegate search to a branching engine only if it supplies: a node state defining a relaxation and logical restrictions; a branching oracle producing finitely many child restrictions exhaustive for the parent feasible set; sound propagation and infeasibility certificates; valid node lower bounds for minimization; and a translation from terminal node solutions to solutions of the original model. The engine may control node selection, branching order, and incumbent management, but it must prune only by certified infeasibility, certified dominance by the incumbent, or completed optimization. Under this contract, delegation preserves global correctness independently of the engine's search order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Delegation is correct when branching is exhaustive, inference and bounds are valid, pruning is certified, and terminal solutions map back to the original model.
assumptions_latex: The original problem is a minimization problem.
Every terminal solution is translated without changing feasibility or objective value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If the delegated finite search terminates with all nodes fathomed, its best incumbent is globally optimal, or certified infeasibility is established.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y\) be a finite nonempty set of master assignments, let \(c:Y\to\mathbb{R}\) be the master cost, and let \(v(y)\) be the optimal value of the subordinate problem fixed at \(y\), with \(v(y)=+\infty\) when that problem is infeasible. The master minimizes \(c(y)+\eta\) over \(y\in Y\) subject to accumulated cuts. At an assignment \(y^k\), the subordinate oracle returns either an optimal subordinate solution and a valid optimality cut \(\eta\geq B_k(y)\) satisfying \(B_k(y)\leq v(y)\) for every \(y\in Y\) and \(B_k(y^k)=v(y^k)\), or a valid feasibility cut satisfied by every assignment with a feasible subordinate problem and violated by \(y^k\). Update the incumbent after a feasible evaluation and stop when the master lower bound equals the incumbent value.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The feasible set is \(\{(0,0)\}\cup\bigl([0,U]\times\{1\}\bigr)\), with objective contribution \(fy+c(x)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\geq0\) be a finite activity upper bound, let \(f\geq0\) be a fixed charge, let \(c:[0,U]\to\mathbb{R}\) be a variable-cost function, and let \(y\in\{0,1\}\) be an activation variable. For an activity level \(x\), the fixed-charge model imposes \(0\leq x\leq Uy\) and contributes \(fy+c(x)\) to the objective. Thus \(y=0\) forces \(x=0\), whereas \(x>0\) forces \(y=1\) and incurs the charge \(f\). If \(y=1\), every \(x\in[0,U]\) is permitted. The formulation permits \(x=0,y=1\); therefore, exact equivalence between activation and strictly positive activity requires an additional positive lower-activity threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A binary variable activates a bounded nonnegative activity and adds a fixed objective charge; positive activity forces activation, although activation remains permitted at zero activity.

knowledge_statements.title: Optional-Activity Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Disjunctive representation of an activity that may be absent or active.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) describe admissible active states and assume \(0\notin X\). An optional activity is represented by the disjunction \([y=0,\ x=0]\vee[y=1,\ x\in X]\), where \(y\in\{0,1\}\). Hence the projected activity set is \(\{0\}\cup X\), and \(y\) records which alternative holds. If \(X\) is described by bounds \(\ell_i\leq x_i\leq u_i\), the linear implications \(\ell_i y\leq x_i\leq u_i y\) represent the on/off bounds; additional constraints defining \(X\) must also be activated conditionally.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An optional activity is either absent at the zero state or present in its active-state set, with a binary variable selecting the alternative.
assumptions_latex: \(0\notin X\), so the alternatives are distinguishable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x,y)\in(\{0\}\times\{0\})\cup(X\times\{1\})\), and the projection onto \(x\) is \(\{0\}\cup X\).

children.title: Scheduling Disjunctions
children.top_down_role: Disjunctive structures governing assignment or timing choices in schedules.

knowledge_statements.title: Scheduling Disjunctions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pairwise temporal-order disjunction for two nonpreemptive activities sharing one unary resource.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For activities \(i\) and \(j\) with start times \(s_i,s_j\) and nonnegative processing times \(p_i,p_j\), exclusive use of one unary resource is represented by \([s_i+p_i\leq s_j]\vee[s_j+p_j\leq s_i]\). The first alternative schedules \(i\) before \(j\); the second schedules \(j\) before \(i\). Equality permits one activity to start exactly when the other finishes. Together with release times, deadlines, and any precedence constraints, imposing this disjunction for every conflicting pair excludes all positive-length overlap between activities using the resource.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two conflicting nonpreemptive activities must be ordered: either the first finishes before the second starts or conversely.
assumptions_latex: Activities \(i\) and \(j\) cannot use the resource simultaneously.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The occupied intervals \([s_i,s_i+p_i)\) and \([s_j,s_j+p_j)\) are disjoint.

children.top_down_role: Alternative precedence structures for activities sharing resources.

assumptions_latex: Each modeled conflicting pair is prohibited from overlapping.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For the pair \(i,j\), exactly one binary order indicator equals one, and the temporal inequality associated with that selected indicator is enforced.

notation.meaning: Indicator that activity i is selected to precede activity j.
Nonnegative processing time of activity i.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary representation of the two selectable orders for a conflicting activity pair.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For distinct conflicting activities \(i\) and \(j\), introduce \(y_{ij},y_{ji}\in\{0,1\}\), where \(y_{ij}=1\) selects the assertion that \(i\) precedes \(j\). Enforce \(y_{ij}+y_{ji}=1\) together with \(y_{ij}=1\Rightarrow s_i+p_i\leq s_j\) and \(y_{ji}=1\Rightarrow s_j+p_j\leq s_i\). Exactly one order indicator is selected for the pair, and its temporal inequality is enforced. For three or more activities with strictly positive processing times, feasible temporal inequalities rule out directed precedence cycles. If zero-duration activities are allowed, temporal feasibility alone can permit cycles among them, so explicit acyclicity or transitivity constraints may be required when the selected indicators themselves must form a global strict order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complementary binary indicators select one temporal inequality for each conflicting pair; positive durations make directed timing cycles infeasible, while zero-duration activities can require explicit acyclicity constraints.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact pairwise nonoverlap condition for half-open processing intervals with positive durations.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let activity \(i\) occupy the half-open interval \(I_i=[s_i,s_i+p_i)\) and activity \(j\) occupy \(I_j=[s_j,s_j+p_j)\), where \(s_i,s_j\in\mathbb{R}\) and \(p_i,p_j>0\). Pairwise nonoverlap is the condition \(I_i\cap I_j=\varnothing\). For these positive-length half-open intervals, this condition is equivalent to \((s_i+p_i\leq s_j)\vee(s_j+p_j\leq s_i)\). The two alternatives cannot both hold, and endpoint equality represents immediate succession without simultaneous resource use.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two positive-length half-open activity intervals are disjoint exactly when one activity finishes no later than the other starts.

knowledge_statements.title: Temporal Ordering Encodings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-activity, bounded-horizon nonoverlap encoding with one ordering variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let activities have start times \(s_i,s_j\), durations \(p_i,p_j>0\), and valid upper bounds \(M_{ij},M_{ji}\) on the corresponding precedence violations. Introduce \(y_{ij}\in\{0,1\}\) and impose \[s_i+p_i\le s_j+M_{ij}(1-y_{ij}),\qquad s_j+p_j\le s_i+M_{ji}y_{ij}.\] When \(y_{ij}=1\), activity \(i\) precedes \(j\); when \(y_{ij}=0\), activity \(j\) precedes \(i\). With valid constants, the integer feasible set is exactly the temporal disjunction \((s_i+p_i\le s_j)\lor(s_j+p_j\le s_i)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A binary ordering variable selects which of two activities precedes the other, producing an exact nonoverlap model when the big-M bounds are valid.
assumptions_latex: Start times have finite bounds yielding valid \(M_{ij},M_{ji}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(s_i+p_i\le s_j)\lor(s_j+p_j\le s_i).\]

notation.meaning: Start time and duration of activity i.

children.title: Piecewise-Regime Models
children.top_down_role: Modeling interfaces for selecting among function segments or operating regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Piecewise-Regime Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite exclusive selection among regime-specific domains and response laws.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\) be a finite regime set, with domains \(D_k\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and functions \(f_k:D_k\to\mathbb R^m\). A piecewise-regime relation is represented by binary variables \(z_k\in\{0,1\}\) satisfying \(\sum_{k\in K}z_k=1\), together with the indicator constraints \[z_k=1\ \Longrightarrow\ x\in D_k\ \text{ and }\ y=f_k(x),\qquad k\in K.\] Its projection onto \((x,y)\) is exactly \(\bigcup_{k\in K}\{(x,f_k(x)):x\in D_k\}\). Discontinuities between adjacent regimes are permitted because no agreement of the functions at shared boundaries is imposed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exactly one binary-selected regime determines both the admissible domain of x and the corresponding response law, allowing discontinuities between regimes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(x,y)\in\bigcup_{k\in K}\{(u,f_k(u)):u\in D_k\}.\]

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite indicator representation and its projection claim are coherent and appropriately classified, but no cited source supports the exactness and discontinuity statements.

children.title: Discontinuous-Domain Models
children.top_down_role: Modeling interfaces for variables or activities restricted to separated domain regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Discontinuous-Domain Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact disaggregated formulation of a finite union of bounded intervals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the admissible scalar domain be \(D=\bigcup_{k=1}^K[\ell_k,u_k]\), where every interval is nonempty and bounded. Introduce \(z_k\in\{0,1\}\) and disaggregated variables \(x_k\in\mathbb R\), and impose \[\sum_{k=1}^Kz_k=1,\qquad x=\sum_{k=1}^Kx_k,\qquad \ell_kz_k\le x_k\le u_kz_k\quad(k=1,\ldots,K).\] For integer \(z\), precisely one disaggregated component is selected, so the projection onto \(x\) equals \(D\). The intervals may overlap or may be separated by forbidden gaps.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Binary selection and disaggregated variables represent a finite union of bounded intervals exactly. One interval is selected as a witness, while the represented value may belong to multiple overlapping intervals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[x\in\bigcup_{k=1}^K[\ell_k,u_k].\]

children.title: Segment Adjacency Structures
children.top_down_role: Adjacency restrictions governing compatible neighboring segments.

knowledge_statements.title: Segment Adjacency Structures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: SOS2 adjacency condition for interpolation over ordered breakpoints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(t_1<\cdots<t_K\) be ordered breakpoints. An SOS2 interpolation vector satisfies \[\lambda_k\ge0,\qquad \sum_{k=1}^K\lambda_k=1,\qquad \bigl|\{k:\lambda_k>0\}\bigr|\le2,\] and whenever \(\lambda_i>0\) and \(\lambda_j>0\), one has \(|i-j|\le1\). With \(x=\sum_{k=1}^K t_k\lambda_k\), the positive weights therefore locate \(x\) within one breakpoint segment. For associated values \(v_k\), setting \(y=\sum_{k=1}^K v_k\lambda_k\) gives linear interpolation on that selected segment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SOS2 weights are nonnegative, sum to one, and have support on at most two adjacent breakpoints, thereby selecting one interpolation segment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[x\in[t_i,t_{i+1}]\ \text{for some }\ i\in\{1,\ldots,K-1\}.\]

notation.meaning: Function value associated with breakpoint k.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The SOS2 adjacency condition is precise, matches the condition container, and supports the interpolation statement, but the record supplies no source citation.

children.title: Disconnected-Region Selection
children.top_down_role: Alternative-selection structures for feasible regions separated by gaps.

knowledge_statements.title: Disconnected-Region Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact extended formulation for selecting one bounded polyhedral region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(k\in K\), let \(P_k=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:A_kx\le b_k\}\) be a nonempty bounded polyhedron. Introduce \(z_k\in\{0,1\}\) and \(x^k\in\mathbb R^n\), and impose \[\sum_{k\in K}z_k=1,\qquad x=\sum_{k\in K}x^k,\qquad A_kx^k\le b_kz_k\quad(k\in K).\] Boundedness makes \(x^k=0\) when \(z_k=0\); the selected component satisfies \(x^k\in P_k\). Consequently, the projection of the integer formulation onto \(x\) is exactly \(\bigcup_{k\in K}P_k\), whether or not the regions touch.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A one-hot selector and region-specific variable copies model membership in exactly one of finitely many bounded, possibly disconnected polyhedra.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[x\in\bigcup_{k\in K}P_k.\]

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The disaggregated formulation is valid for nonempty bounded polyhedra because boundedness gives a trivial recession cone. Its exact projection claim nevertheless lacks a cited source and locator.

children.title: Exclusive-Regime Complementarity Model Family
children.top_down_role: Mutually exclusive regimes and complementarity structures represented through disjunctions.

children.title: Either–Or Regime Models
children.top_down_role: Modeling interfaces for choices between mutually exclusive operating regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Either–Or Regime Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary indicator representation of a two-branch exclusive disjunction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and let \(g_0,g_1:X\to\mathbb R\). Introduce \(z\in\{0,1\}\) and impose the indicator constraints \[z=0\ \Longrightarrow\ g_0(x)\le0,\qquad z=1\ \Longrightarrow\ g_1(x)\le0,\qquad x\in X.\] The projection onto \(x\) equals \(\{x\in X:g_0(x)\le0\}\cup\{x\in X:g_1(x)\le0\}\). If both regimes are feasible at the same \(x\), either selector value may be used; exclusivity concerns the chosen branch, not necessarily disjointness of the branch feasible sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One binary variable selects which of two regime constraints is enforced; overlapping feasible regimes remain allowed unless additional exclusivity is imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[x\in\{u\in X:g_0(u)\le0\}\cup\{u\in X:g_1(u)\le0\}.\]

notation.meaning: Constraint functions for the two regimes.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The binary indicator formulation correctly represents the union and properly distinguishes selector exclusivity from disjoint branch sets, but no source is cited.

children.title: Complementarity Models
children.top_down_role: Modeling interfaces for paired quantities subject to exclusive activity.

knowledge_statements.title: Complementarity Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise complementarity for two nonnegative vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For vectors \(u,v\in\mathbb R^m\), the complementarity relation \(0\le u\perp v\ge0\) means \[u_i\ge0,\qquad v_i\ge0,\qquad u_iv_i=0\quad(i=1,\ldots,m).\] Equivalently, \(u\ge0\), \(v\ge0\), and \(u^{\mathsf T}v=0\). Thus, for each component, at least one member of the pair is zero, while both may be zero. The relation is an orthogonality condition restricted to the nonnegative orthant and generally defines a nonconvex feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two nonnegative vectors are complementary when each component pair has zero product; both members of a pair may simultaneously be zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[0\le u\perp v\ge0\ \Longleftrightarrow\ u\ge0,\ v\ge0,\ u^{\mathsf T}v=0.\]

notation.meaning: Euclidean inner product of u and v.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The componentwise definition and inner-product equivalence are correct for nonnegative vectors and fit a definition container, but the record has no supporting citation.

children.title: Mutual-Exclusion Encodings
children.top_down_role: Encoding families shared by exclusive-regime and complementarity structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Mutual-Exclusion Encodings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact bounded binary encoding of scalar nonnegative complementarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(u,v\ge0\) have valid finite upper bounds \(U,V\). Introduce \(z\in\{0,1\}\) and impose \[0\le u\le Uz,
\qquad 0\le v\le V(1-z).\] If \(z=0\), then \(u=0\); if \(z=1\), then \(v=0\). Hence the projection onto \((u,v)\) is exactly \(\{(u,v):0\le u\le U,\ 0\le v\le V,\ uv=0\}\). The formulation permits \(u=v=0\), for which either binary value is feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite upper bounds permit an exact binary encoding in which at most one of two nonnegative variables can be positive.

notation.meaning: Valid finite upper bounds for u and v.
Binary variable selecting which quantity may be positive.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bounded scalar complementarity encoding is mathematically exact and appropriately classified as a representation, but no source or locator is supplied.

children.title: Complementarity Reformulation Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits of disjunctive reformulations for complementarity-based models.

knowledge_statements.title: Complementarity Reformulation Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-bound requirement for exact big-M complementarity reformulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^2\) describe the surrounding constraints and let \[F=\{(u,v)\in X:u\ge0,\ v\ge0,\ uv=0\}.\] Retaining \((u,v)\in X\), the binary inequalities \[0\le u\le Uz,\qquad 0\le v\le V(1-z),\qquad z\in\{0,1\},\] project exactly onto \(F\) only if \(U\) and \(V\) are valid upper bounds for \(u\) and \(v\) on \(F\). If \(u\) or \(v\) is unbounded above on \(F\), no finite constant can preserve the corresponding complementary branch. A finite constant below a valid bound truncates feasible points; an unnecessarily large but valid constant preserves the integer projection while generally weakening the continuous relaxation relative to a tighter valid constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact big-M complementarity reformulation requires valid finite coordinate bounds over the surrounding feasible set. Too-small constants truncate feasible branches, whereas overly large but valid constants weaken the relaxation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\sup\{u:(u,v)\in F\}=\infty\ \Longrightarrow\ \text{no finite exact upper bound }U.\]

notation.meaning: Set defined by the surrounding constraints.

children.title: Process Superstructure Models
children.top_down_role: Hierarchical alternatives and optional subsystems in process design.

knowledge_statements.title: Process Superstructure Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hierarchical activation formulation for optional process units and alternatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a process superstructure be a directed graph with candidate units \(i\in N\), flows \(q_a\) on arcs \(a\in A\), and activation variables \(y_i\in\{0,1\}\). Valid capacity constraints have the form \(0\le q_a\le U_a y_i\) when arc \(a\) belongs to unit \(i\). If unit \(j\) requires parent unit \(i\), impose \(y_j\le y_i\). For a mutually exclusive child set \(C(i)\), impose \(\sum_{j\in C(i)}y_j\le y_i\), or equality when exactly one child must operate whenever the parent is active. Material and energy balances are imposed on activated flows.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Binary unit activations, conditional capacities, hierarchy constraints, and alternative-child constraints encode optional subsystems within a process superstructure.
assumptions_latex: Every \(U_a\) is a valid finite flow bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[y_j\le y_i\quad(j\text{ requires }i),\qquad \sum_{j\in C(i)}y_j\le y_i.\]

notation.meaning: Binary activation of candidate unit i.
Mutually exclusive children of unit i.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation matches the process-superstructure container and its hierarchy and mutual-exclusion inequalities are coherent, but the domain-specific modeling claims require a process-systems source with an exact locator.

children.title: Implementation Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Structural, numerical, and size-related boundaries encountered during compilation and solver processing.

children.title: Premature Structure Flattening
children.top_down_role: Loss of hierarchy and alternative-local information before solver processing.

knowledge_statements.title: Premature Structure Flattening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relaxation loss caused by replacing branch-local structure with loose global constants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The disjunction \((z=0\land x=0)\lor(z=1\land x=1)\) has convex hull \(x=z\) with \(0\le z\le1\). A flattened big-M encoding may instead impose \[-Mz\le x\le Mz,\qquad -M(1-z)\le x-1\le M(1-z),\qquad z\in\{0,1\}.\] It is integer-exact for \(M\ge1\), but when \(M>1\) its continuous relaxation admits points outside \(x=z\); for example, \(z=1/2\) permits an interval of \(x\)-values. Thus discarding alternative-local equalities before reformulation can strictly weaken the relaxation despite preserving integer feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Flattening branch-local equalities into loose global big-M constraints can preserve integer feasibility while producing a strictly weaker continuous relaxation.
assumptions_latex: The binary restriction is relaxed to \(0\le z\le1\) for relaxation comparison.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname{proj}_{x,z}(R_M)\supsetneq\{(x,z):x=z,\ 0\le z\le1\}.\]

notation.meaning: Continuous relaxation of the flattened formulation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The example correctly shows integer exactness for M at least one and a strict relaxation gap for M greater than one, and it fits a failure-boundary container. No source is cited for the broader structure-flattening interpretation.

children.title: Strong Relaxations with Excessive Overhead
children.top_down_role: Extended models whose strength is offset by size or processing cost.

knowledge_statements.title: Strong Relaxations with Excessive Overhead
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Size boundary for disaggregated convex-hull formulations of many alternatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a union of \(K\) polyhedra in \(\mathbb R^n\), a standard disaggregated formulation introduces one vector copy \(x^k\in\mathbb R^n\) and one selector \(z_k\) for each alternative. If alternative \(k\) has \(m_k\) inequalities, the explicit construction has \(Kn\) copied continuous variables, \(K\) selectors, \(\sum_{k=1}^K m_k\) scaled alternative inequalities, \(n\) componentwise linking equalities, and one selector-sum equality, apart from constraints already present outside the disjunction. Thus formulation size grows with the number and dimension of the alternatives. Even when its continuous relaxation is ideal, the enlarged model can increase construction, presolve, factorization, node-processing, and memory costs, so relaxation strength alone does not guarantee a lower total solution time.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A disaggregated formulation can provide an ideal relaxation while adding one full variable copy and one selector per alternative. Its larger model may impose processing and memory costs that outweigh reductions in search.
assumptions_latex: \(K<\infty\) explicitly represented polyhedral alternatives are given.
Alternative \(k\) is described by \(m_k\) inequalities in \(n\) variables.
The count refers to the stated disaggregated construction and excludes constraints external to the disjunction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[N_{\mathrm{copied\,var}}=Kn,\qquad N_{\mathrm{selector}}=K,\qquad N_{\mathrm{listed\,con}}=n+1+\sum_{k=1}^K m_k.\]

notation.meaning: Number of inequalities describing alternative k.
Continuous variable copy for alternative k.

children.title: Logical–Numerical Feasibility Mismatch
children.top_down_role: Disagreement between intended logical semantics and tolerance-based feasibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Logical–Numerical Feasibility Mismatch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Big-M implication under absolute row and integrality tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the intended implication “if the binary variable is zero, then the continuous variable is zero,” encoded by \(0\le x\le My\), where \(M>0\) and \(y\in\{0,1\}\). Suppose an implementation regards \(\widehat y\) as zero whenever \(|\widehat y|\le\tau_I\), and accepts the row whenever \(\widehat x-M\widehat y\le\tau_F\), with \(\tau_I>0\) and \(\tau_F\ge0\). The point \((\widehat x,\widehat y)=(M\tau_I,\tau_I)\) satisfies the implemented row exactly and is interpreted as having \(y=0\), yet \(\widehat x>0\). Thus numerical acceptance need not imply satisfaction of the intended logical implication; the possible semantic violation scales as \(M\tau_I+\tau_F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With integrality and row tolerances, a big-M constraint can be numerically feasible while violating its interpreted implication; the discrepancy can grow proportionally to the big-M coefficient.
assumptions_latex: Values within \(\tau_I\) of zero are logically interpreted as zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\widehat x,\widehat y)=(M\tau_I,\tau_I)\) is numerically accepted but violates \(y=0\Rightarrow x=0\), with potential discrepancy bounded in scale by \(M\tau_I+\tau_F\).

source_refs.locator: 1.3 Inequality Systems with Logical Connectives p. 6
3.4.4 Modal formulation p. 38

source_witnesses.locator: 1.3 Inequality Systems with Logical Connectives p. 6
3.4.4 Modal formulation p. 38

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind fits the terminal container, and the conditional construction is mathematically coherent. However, the cited sections concern logical or modal formulations and do not specifically support the stated integrality interpretation rule, row-feasibility rule, or the resulting M\tau_I+\tau_F discrepancy. A source with a specific locator for solver feasibility and integrality tolerances is required before this numerical failure claim can be accepted.

children.title: Auxiliary Representation Explosion
children.top_down_role: Excessive growth from disaggregation, normalization, or explicit pattern representation.

assumptions_latex: For each \(k\in\{1,\ldots,K\}\), \(P_k=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:A_kx\le b_k\}\) is a nonempty polytope and \(A_k\) has \(m_k\) rows.
The formulation explicitly disaggregates every disjunct.
The Boolean-pattern normalization retains all \(2^p\) assignments, where \(p\) is a nonnegative integer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: When \(K=2^p\), explicit disaggregation introduces \(2^pn+2^p\) auxiliary variables and therefore has size \(\Omega(2^pn)\).

notation.meaning: number of rows of the matrix associated with disjunct k
number of Boolean atoms whose assignments are enumerated

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Size growth of explicit disjunctive-hull and Boolean-pattern representations.

source_refs.locator: 2.1.1 Tightness of the Lifted Representation p. 22
1.4 The Combinatorial Explosion p. 8

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(k\in\{1,\ldots,K\}\), let \(P_k=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:A_kx\le b_k\}\) be a nonempty polytope, with \(A_k\) having \(m_k\) rows. The standard disaggregated convex-hull representation introduces auxiliary variables \(x^k\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(\lambda_k\ge0\), and imposes \(x=\sum_{k=1}^K x^k\), \(A_kx^k\le b_k\lambda_k\) for every \(k\in\{1,\ldots,K\}\), and \(\sum_{k=1}^K\lambda_k=1\). It introduces \(Kn+K\) auxiliary variables. Counting the \(K\) nonnegativity bounds on \(\lambda_k\) as inequalities, it displays \(\sum_{k=1}^K m_k+n+K+1\) equality-or-inequality rows. If an explicit normalization enumerates every assignment of \(p\) Boolean atoms, then \(K=2^p\), and the number of auxiliary variables is \(2^pn+2^p=\Omega(2^pn)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Disaggregation grows linearly with the number of explicitly represented disjuncts. If all assignments of p Boolean atoms are enumerated, there are 2^p disjuncts, so the auxiliary-variable count is exponential in p.
